## [◆](#ab0233c2d867cbd561036ed2440a4fec0)SFML\_DEFINE\_DISCRETE\_GPU\_PREFERENCE

|  |
| --- |
| #define SFML\_DEFINE\_DISCRETE\_GPU\_PREFERENCE |

A macro to encourage usage of the discrete GPU.

In order to inform the Nvidia/AMD driver that an SFML application could benefit from using the more powerful discrete GPU, special symbols have to be publicly exported from the final executable.

SFML defines a helper macro to easily do this.

Place SFML\_DEFINE\_DISCRETE\_GPU\_PREFERENCE in the global scope of a source file that will be linked into the final executable. Typically it is best to place it where the main function is also defined.

Definition at line [68](GpuPreference_8hpp_source.html#l00068) of file [GpuPreference.hpp](GpuPreference_8hpp_source.html).

## Detailed Description

Represents an angle value.

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html "Represents an angle value.") encapsulates an angle value in a flexible way.

It allows for defining an angle value either as a number of degrees or radians. It also works the other way around. You can read an angle value as either a number of degrees or radians.

By using such a flexible interface, the API doesn't impose any fixed type or unit for angle values and lets the user choose their own preferred representation.

[Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html "Represents an angle value.") values support the usual mathematical operations. You can add or subtract two angles, multiply or divide an angle by a number, compare two angles, etc.

Usage example:

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a1 = [sf::degrees](namespacesf.html#a956d8e2dd821777ce475c0856bfa879d)(90);

float [radians](#a8738691f6b62b7fcebf5c7e9b47c4a24) = a1.[asRadians](#a2e5b70ac8b02cd528deb652b25d3137f)(); // 1.5708f

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a2 = [sf::radians](namespacesf.html#a893b41868f0fb30e52e6490e3f5524b3)(3.141592654f);

float [degrees](#a97d979192b0069419fec49a8135f137b) = a2.[asDegrees](#ae724c2b5595a2b4423cdba21ac229c67)(); // 180.0f

using namespace [sf::Literals](namespacesf_1_1Literals.html);

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a3 = 10\_deg; // 10 degrees

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a4 = 1.5\_deg; // 1.5 degrees

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a5 = 1\_rad; // 1 radians

[sf::Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) a6 = 3.14\_rad; // 3.14 radians

## [◆](#a71452e36bce7d8d9b380f86ff6d72f72)wrapSigned()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) sf::Angle::wrapSigned | ( |  | ) | const | | nodiscardconstexpr |

Wrap to a range such that -180° <= angle < 180°

Similar to a modulo operation, this returns a copy of the angle constrained to the range [-180°, 180°) == [-Pi, Pi). The resulting angle represents a rotation which is equivalent to \*this.

The name "signed" originates from the similarity to signed integers:

|  | signed | unsigned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| char | [-128, 128) | [0, 256) |
| [Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html "Represents an angle value.") | [-180°, 180°) | [0°, 360°) |

Returns
:   Signed angle, wrapped to [-180°, 180°)

See also
:   [wrapUnsigned](#ad83d33d157a5836f406e148dfad66b01 "Wrap to a range such that 0° <= angle < 360°")

Wrap to a range such that 0° <= angle < 360°

Similar to a modulo operation, this returns a copy of the angle constrained to the range [0°, 360°) == [0, Tau) == [0, 2\*Pi). The resulting angle represents a rotation which is equivalent to \*this.

The name "unsigned" originates from the similarity to unsigned integers:

|  | signed | unsigned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| char | [-128, 128) | [0, 256) |
| [Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html "Represents an angle value.") | [-180°, 180°) | [0°, 360°) |

Returns
:   Unsigned angle, wrapped to [0°, 360°)

## Detailed Description

Base class for classes that require an audio device.

This class is for internal use only, it must be the base of every class that requires a valid audio device in order to work.

Definition at line [41](AudioResource_8hpp_source.html#l00041) of file [AudioResource.hpp](AudioResource_8hpp_source.html).

## Detailed Description

Specialized shape representing a circle.

This class inherits all the functions of [sf::Transformable](classsf_1_1Transformable.html "Decomposed transform defined by a position, a rotation and a scale.") (position, rotation, scale, bounds, ...) as well as the functions of [sf::Shape](classsf_1_1Shape.html "Base class for textured shapes with outline.") (outline, color, texture, ...).

Usage example:

[sf::CircleShape](classsf_1_1CircleShape.html) circle;

circle.[setRadius](#a21cdf85fc2f201e10222a241af864be0)(150);

circle.[setOutlineColor](classsf_1_1Shape.html#a7dbbed35b7544a9e592acd3908713256)([sf::Color::Red](classsf_1_1Color.html#a127dbf55db9c07d0fa8f4bfcbb97594a));

circle.[setOutlineThickness](classsf_1_1Shape.html#a5ad336ad74fc1f567fce3b7e44cf87dc)(5);

circle.[setPosition](classsf_1_1Transformable.html#a47c1375b57cbb0e513286e8d11f6dd4d)({10, 20});

...

window.draw(circle);

[sf::CircleShape](classsf_1_1CircleShape.html)

Specialized shape representing a circle.

set the position of the object

Since the graphics card can't draw perfect circles, we have to fake them with multiple triangles connected to each other. The "points count" property of [sf::CircleShape](classsf_1_1CircleShape.html "Specialized shape representing a circle.") defines how many of these triangles to use, and therefore defines the quality of the circle.

The number of points can also be used for another purpose; with small numbers you can create any regular polygon shape: equilateral triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, ...

See also
:   [sf::Shape](classsf_1_1Shape.html "Base class for textured shapes with outline."), [sf::RectangleShape](classsf_1_1RectangleShape.html "Specialized shape representing a rectangle."), [sf::ConvexShape](classsf_1_1ConvexShape.html "Specialized shape representing a convex polygon.")

## [◆](#ac0e29425d908d5442060cc44790fe4da)getGlobalBounds()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [FloatRect](namespacesf.html#a701020eb396e62ba560619e68c689a38) sf::Shape::getGlobalBounds | ( |  | ) | const | | nodiscardinherited |

Get the global (non-minimal) bounding rectangle of the entity.

The returned rectangle is in global coordinates, which means that it takes into account the transformations (translation, rotation, scale, ...) that are applied to the entity. In other words, this function returns the bounds of the shape in the global 2D world's coordinate system.

This function does not necessarily return the *minimal* bounding rectangle. It merely ensures that the returned rectangle covers all the vertices (but possibly more). This allows for a fast approximation of the bounds as a first check; you may want to use more precise checks on top of that.

Returns
:   Global bounding rectangle of the entity

| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::Shape::setTexture | ( | const [Texture](classsf_1_1Texture.html) \* | *texture*, | |  |  | bool | *resetRect* = false ) | | inherited |

Change the source texture of the shape.

The texture argument refers to a texture that must exist as long as the shape uses it. Indeed, the shape doesn't store its own copy of the texture, but rather keeps a pointer to the one that you passed to this function. If the source texture is destroyed and the shape tries to use it, the behavior is undefined. texture can be a null pointer to disable texturing. If resetRect is true, the TextureRect property of the shape is automatically adjusted to the size of the new texture. If it is false, the texture rect is left unchanged.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | texture | New texture |
    | resetRect | Should the texture rect be reset to the size of the new texture? |

## Detailed Description

Utility class that measures the elapsed time.

[sf::Clock](classsf_1_1Clock.html "Utility class that measures the elapsed time.") is a lightweight class for measuring time.

The clock starts automatically after being constructed.

It provides the most precise time that the underlying OS can achieve (generally microseconds or nanoseconds). It also ensures monotonicity, which means that the returned time can never go backward, even if the system time is changed.

Usage example:

[sf::Clock](classsf_1_1Clock.html) clock;

...

Time time1 = clock.[getElapsedTime](#abe889b42a65bcd8eefc16419645d08a7)();

...

[Time](classsf_1_1Time.html#ac71085f83ee2bd74e005fc63d7a47a41) time2 = clock.[restart](#a123e2627f2943e5ecaa1db0c7df3231b)();

...

[Time](classsf_1_1Time.html#ac71085f83ee2bd74e005fc63d7a47a41) time3 = clock.[reset](#a564522bc9caf98b412aa0c6f39a81d75)();

[sf::Clock](classsf_1_1Clock.html)

## Detailed Description

Utility class for manipulating RGBA colors.

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html "Utility class for manipulating RGBA colors.") is a simple color class composed of 4 components:

* Red
* Green
* Blue
* Alpha (opacity)

Each component is a public member, an unsigned integer in the range [0, 255]. Thus, colors can be constructed and manipulated very easily:

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html) color(255, 0, 0); // red

color.r = 0; // make it black

color.b = 128; // make it dark blue

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html)

Utility class for manipulating RGBA colors.

**Definition** [Color.hpp:40](Color_8hpp_source.html#l00039)

The fourth component of colors, named "alpha", represents the opacity of the color. A color with an alpha value of 255 will be fully opaque, while an alpha value of 0 will make a color fully transparent, whatever the value of the other components is.

The most common colors are already defined as static variables:

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html) black = [sf::Color::Black](#a77c688197b981338f0b19dc58bd2facd);

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html) white = [sf::Color::White](#a4fd874712178d9e206f53226002aa4ca);

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html) red = [sf::Color::Red](#a127dbf55db9c07d0fa8f4bfcbb97594a);

## Detailed Description

Class holding a valid drawing context.

If you need to make OpenGL calls without having an active window (like in a thread), you can use an instance of this class to get a valid context.

Having a valid context is necessary for *every* OpenGL call.

Note that a context is only active in its current thread, if you create a new thread it will have no valid context by default.

To use a [sf::Context](classsf_1_1Context.html "Class holding a valid drawing context.") instance, just construct it and let it live as long as you need a valid context. No explicit activation is needed, all it has to do is to exist. Its destructor will take care of deactivating and freeing all the attached resources.

Usage example:

void threadFunction(void\*)

{

[sf::Context](classsf_1_1Context.html) context;

// from now on, you have a valid context

// you can make OpenGL calls

glClear(GL\_DEPTH\_BUFFER\_BIT);

}

// the context is automatically deactivated and destroyed

// by the sf::Context destructor

[sf::Context](classsf_1_1Context.html)

## Detailed Description

Specialized shape representing a convex polygon.

This class inherits all the functions of [sf::Transformable](classsf_1_1Transformable.html "Decomposed transform defined by a position, a rotation and a scale.") (position, rotation, scale, bounds, ...) as well as the functions of [sf::Shape](classsf_1_1Shape.html "Base class for textured shapes with outline.") (outline, color, texture, ...).

It is important to keep in mind that a convex shape must always be... convex, otherwise it may not be drawn correctly. Moreover, the points must be defined in order; using a random order would result in an incorrect shape.

Usage example:

[sf::ConvexShape](classsf_1_1ConvexShape.html) polygon;

polygon.[setPointCount](#a56e6e79ade6dd651cc1a0e39cb68deae)(3);

polygon.[setPoint](#a24eccc14ac5589e05f9f7cdbc6decf2c)(0, [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(0, 0));

polygon.[setPoint](#a24eccc14ac5589e05f9f7cdbc6decf2c)(1, [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(0, 10));

polygon.[setPoint](#a24eccc14ac5589e05f9f7cdbc6decf2c)(2, [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(25, 5));

polygon.[setOutlineColor](classsf_1_1Shape.html#a7dbbed35b7544a9e592acd3908713256)([sf::Color::Red](classsf_1_1Color.html#a127dbf55db9c07d0fa8f4bfcbb97594a));

polygon.[setOutlineThickness](classsf_1_1Shape.html#a5ad336ad74fc1f567fce3b7e44cf87dc)(5);

polygon.[setPosition](classsf_1_1Transformable.html#a47c1375b57cbb0e513286e8d11f6dd4d)({10, 20});

...

window.draw(polygon);

## [◆](#ac0e29425d908d5442060cc44790fe4da)getGlobalBounds()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [FloatRect](namespacesf.html#a701020eb396e62ba560619e68c689a38) sf::Shape::getGlobalBounds | ( |  | ) | const | | nodiscardinherited |

Get the global (non-minimal) bounding rectangle of the entity.

The returned rectangle is in global coordinates, which means that it takes into account the transformations (translation, rotation, scale, ...) that are applied to the entity. In other words, this function returns the bounds of the shape in the global 2D world's coordinate system.

This function does not necessarily return the *minimal* bounding rectangle. It merely ensures that the returned rectangle covers all the vertices (but possibly more). This allows for a fast approximation of the bounds as a first check; you may want to use more precise checks on top of that.

Returns
:   Global bounding rectangle of the entity

The origin of an object defines the center point for all transformations (position, scale, rotation). The coordinates of this point must be relative to the top-left corner of the object, and ignore all transformations (position, scale, rotation). The default origin of a transformable object is (0, 0).

## [◆](#af8fb22bab1956325be5d62282711e3b6)setTexture()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::Shape::setTexture | ( | const [Texture](classsf_1_1Texture.html) \* | *texture*, | |  |  | bool | *resetRect* = false ) | | inherited |

Change the source texture of the shape.

The texture argument refers to a texture that must exist as long as the shape uses it. Indeed, the shape doesn't store its own copy of the texture, but rather keeps a pointer to the one that you passed to this function. If the source texture is destroyed and the shape tries to use it, the behavior is undefined. texture can be a null pointer to disable texturing. If resetRect is true, the TextureRect property of the shape is automatically adjusted to the size of the new texture. If it is false, the texture rect is left unchanged.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | texture | New texture |
    | resetRect | Should the texture rect be reset to the size of the new texture? |

See also

## Detailed Description

[Cursor](classsf_1_1Cursor.html "Cursor defines the appearance of a system cursor.") defines the appearance of a system cursor.

Warning
:   Features related to [Cursor](classsf_1_1Cursor.html "Cursor defines the appearance of a system cursor.") are not supported on iOS and Android.

This class abstracts the operating system resources associated with either a native system cursor or a custom cursor.

After loading the cursor graphical appearance with either [createFromPixels()](#a93aa2dfcc8c4f27513c6632153521fa7 "Create a cursor with the provided image.") or [createFromSystem()](#a3385d2f53bc5b3b296f0409f79a57116 "Create a native system cursor."), the cursor can be changed with [sf::WindowBase::setMouseCursor()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a07487a3c7e04472b19e96d3a602213ec "Set the displayed cursor to a native system cursor.").

The behavior is undefined if the cursor is destroyed while in use by the window.

Usage example:

[sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html) window;

// ... create window as usual ...

const auto cursor = [sf::Cursor::createFromSystem](#a3385d2f53bc5b3b296f0409f79a57116)([sf::Cursor::Type::Hand](#ab9ab152aec1f8a4955e34ccae08f930aaa78b1ac16c0cd02168097fc9a9bd7604)).value();

window.[setMouseCursor](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a07487a3c7e04472b19e96d3a602213ec)(cursor);

|  |  | [Vector2u](namespacesf.html#adc674b5f5c13a6734954a18e01a73b42) | *size*, |
|  |  | [Vector2u](namespacesf.html#adc674b5f5c13a6734954a18e01a73b42) | *hotspot* ) |

Construct a cursor with the provided image.

pixels must be an array of size pixels in 32-bit RGBA format. If not, this will cause undefined behavior.

If pixels is nullptr or either of size's properties are 0, the current cursor is left unchanged and the function will return false.

In addition to specifying the pixel data, you can also specify the location of the hotspot of the cursor. The hotspot is the pixel coordinate within the cursor image which will be located exactly where the mouse pointer position is. Any mouse actions that are performed will return the window/screen location of the hotspot.

Warning
:   On Unix platforms which do not support colored cursors, the pixels are mapped into a monochrome bitmap: pixels with an alpha channel to 0 are transparent, black if the RGB channel are close to zero, and white otherwise.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | pixels | Array of pixels of the image |
    | size | Width and height of the image |
    | hotspot | (x,y) location of the hotspot |

Exceptions
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [sf::Exception](classsf_1_1Exception.html "Library-specific exception type.") | if the cursor could not be constructed |

## Detailed Description

Abstract base class for objects that can be drawn to a render target.

[sf::Drawable](classsf_1_1Drawable.html "Abstract base class for objects that can be drawn to a render target.") is a very simple base class that allows objects of derived classes to be drawn to a [sf::RenderTarget](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html "Base class for all render targets (window, texture, ...)").

All you have to do in your derived class is to override the draw virtual function.

Note that inheriting from [sf::Drawable](classsf_1_1Drawable.html "Abstract base class for objects that can be drawn to a render target.") is not mandatory, but it allows this nice syntax window.draw(object) rather than object.draw(window), which is more consistent with other SFML classes.

Example:

class MyDrawable : public [sf::Drawable](classsf_1_1Drawable.html)

{

public:

...

private:

void [draw](#a90d2c88bba9b035a0844eccb380ef631)([sf::RenderTarget](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html)& target, [sf::RenderStates](structsf_1_1RenderStates.html) states) const override

{

// You can draw other high-level objects

target.[draw](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html#a12417a3bcc245c41d957b29583556f39)(m\_sprite, states);

// ... or use the low-level API

states.[texture](structsf_1_1RenderStates.html#a457fc5a41731889de9cf39cf9b3436c3) = &m\_texture;

target.[draw](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html#a12417a3bcc245c41d957b29583556f39)(m\_vertices, states);

// ... or draw with OpenGL directly

glBegin(GL\_TRIANGLES);

...

glEnd();

}

[sf::Sprite](classsf_1_1Sprite.html) m\_sprite;

[sf::Texture](classsf_1_1Texture.html) m\_texture;

[sf::VertexArray](classsf_1_1VertexArray.html) m\_vertices;

};

## Detailed Description

Defines a system event and its parameters.

[sf::Event](classsf_1_1Event.html "Defines a system event and its parameters.") holds all the information about a system event that just happened.

Events are retrieved using the [sf::Window::pollEvent](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.") and [sf::Window::waitEvent](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it.") functions.

A [sf::Event](classsf_1_1Event.html "Defines a system event and its parameters.") instance contains the subtype of the event (mouse moved, key pressed, window closed, ...) as well as the details about this particular event. Each event corresponds to a different subtype struct which contains the data required to process that event.

[Event](classsf_1_1Event.html "Defines a system event and its parameters.") subtypes are event types belonging to [sf::Event](classsf_1_1Event.html "Defines a system event and its parameters."), such as [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html "Closed event subtype.") or [sf::Event::MouseMoved](structsf_1_1Event_1_1MouseMoved.html "Mouse move event subtype.").

The way to access the current active event subtype is via [sf::Event::getIf](#a2f7d5c82b6401ae288a252c295129a32 "Attempt to get specified event subtype."). This member function returns the address of the event subtype struct if the event subtype matches the active event, otherwise it returns nullptr.

[sf::Event::is](#a40df10cc639742089960c7dbe9144343 "Check current event subtype.") is used to check the active event subtype without actually reading any of the corresponding event data.

while (const std::optional event = window.pollEvent())

{

// Window closed or escape key pressed: exit

if (event->is<[sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)>() ||

(event->is<[sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)>() &&

event->getIf<[sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)>()->[code](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html#a8d0e09b379708f01b22f390810994613) == [sf::Keyboard::Key::Escape](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a013ec032d3460d4be4431c6ab1f8f224)))

window.close();

// The window was resized

if (const auto\* resized = event->getIf<[sf::Event::Resized](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Resized.html)>())

doSomethingWithTheNewSize(resized->size);

// etc ...

}

[sf::Keyboard::Key::Escape](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a013ec032d3460d4be4431c6ab1f8f224)

## Detailed Description

Implementation of input stream based on a file.

This class is a specialization of [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.") that reads from a file on disk.

It wraps a file in the common [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.") interface and therefore allows to use generic classes or functions that accept such a stream, with a file on disk as the data source.

In addition to the virtual functions inherited from [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams."), [FileInputStream](classsf_1_1FileInputStream.html "Implementation of input stream based on a file.") adds a function to specify the file to open.

SFML resource classes can usually be loaded directly from a filename, so this class shouldn't be useful to you unless you create your own algorithms that operate on an [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.").

Usage example:

void process([InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html)& stream);

std::optional stream = [sf::FileInputStream::open](#ab3a62ca25f1e487ce77dc5180e60e33e)("some\_file.dat");

if (stream)

process(\*stream);

[sf::FileInputStream::open](#ab3a62ca25f1e487ce77dc5180e60e33e)

bool open(const std::filesystem::path &filename)

Open the stream from a file path.

## Detailed Description

Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.

Fonts can be opened from a file, from memory or from a custom stream, and supports the most common types of fonts.

See the openFromFile function for the complete list of supported formats.

Once it is opened, a [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") instance provides three types of information about the font:

* Global metrics, such as the line spacing
* Per-glyph metrics, such as bounding box or kerning
* Pixel representation of glyphs

Fonts alone are not very useful: they hold the font data but cannot make anything useful of it. To do so you need to use the [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.") class, which is able to properly output text with several options such as character size, style, color, position, rotation, etc. This separation allows more flexibility and better performances: indeed a [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") is a heavy resource, and any operation on it is slow (often too slow for real-time applications). On the other side, a [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.") is a lightweight object which can combine the glyphs data and metrics of a [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") to display any text on a render target. Note that it is also possible to bind several [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.") instances to the same [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.").

It is important to note that the [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.") instance doesn't copy the font that it uses, it only keeps a reference to it. Thus, a [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") must not be destructed while it is used by a [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.") (i.e. never write a function that uses a local [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") instance for creating a text).

Usage example:

// Open a new font

const [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html) font("arial.ttf");

// Create a text which uses our font

[sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html) text1(font);

text1.setCharacterSize(30);

text1.setStyle([sf::Text::Regular](classsf_1_1Text.html#aa8add4aef484c6e6b20faff07452bd82a2af9ae5e1cda126570f744448e0caa32));

// Create another text using the same font, but with different parameters

[sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html) text2(font);

text2.setCharacterSize(50);

text2.setStyle([sf::Text::Italic](classsf_1_1Text.html#aa8add4aef484c6e6b20faff07452bd82aee249eb803848723c542c2062ebe69d8));

Apart from opening font files, and passing them to instances of [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target."), you should normally not have to deal directly with this class. However, it may be useful to access the font metrics or rasterized glyphs for advanced usage.

Note that if the font is a bitmap font, it is not scalable, thus not all requested sizes will be available to use. This needs to be taken into consideration when using [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target."). If you need to display text of a certain size, make sure the corresponding bitmap font that supports that size is used.

See also
:   [sf::Text](classsf_1_1Text.html "Graphical text that can be drawn to a render target.")

Construct the font from a file.

The supported font formats are: TrueType, Type 1, CFF, OpenType, SFNT, X11 PCF, Windows FNT, BDF, PFR and Type 42. Note that this function knows nothing about the standard fonts installed on the user's system, thus you can't load them directly.

Warning
:   SFML cannot preload all the font data in this function, so the file has to remain accessible until the [sf::Font](classsf_1_1Font.html "Class for loading and manipulating character fonts.") object opens a new font or is destroyed.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | filename | Path of the font file to open |

:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [sf::Exception](classsf_1_1Exception.html "Library-specific exception type.") | if opening was unsuccessful |

Retrieve a glyph of the font.

If the font is a bitmap font, not all character sizes might be available. If the glyph is not available at the requested size, an empty glyph is returned.

You may want to use hasGlyph to determine if the glyph exists before requesting it. If the glyph does not exist, a font specific default is returned.

Be aware that using a negative value for the outline thickness will cause distorted rendering.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | codePoint | Unicode code point of the character to get |
    | characterSize | Reference character size |
    | bold | Retrieve the bold version or the regular one? |
    | outlineThickness | Thickness of outline (when != 0 the glyph will not be filled) |

Returns
:   The glyph corresponding to codePoint and characterSize

## [◆](#ab92c0eb62d334b0f54dfe67d34b25e00)getKerning()

Get the kerning offset of two glyphs.

The kerning is an extra offset (negative) to apply between two glyphs when rendering them, to make the pair look more "natural". For example, the pair "AV" have a special kerning to make them closer than other characters. Most of the glyphs pairs have a kerning offset of zero, though.

    | first | Unicode code point of the first character |
    | second | Unicode code point of the second character |
    | characterSize | Reference character size |
    | bold | Retrieve the bold version or the regular one? |

Returns
:   Kerning value for first and second, in pixels

Determine if this font has a glyph representing the requested code point.

Most fonts only include a very limited selection of glyphs from specific Unicode subsets, like Latin, Cyrillic, or Asian characters.

While code points without representation will return a font specific default character, it might be useful to verify whether specific code points are included to determine whether a font is suited to display text in a specific language.

The supported font formats are: TrueType, Type 1, CFF, OpenType, SFNT, X11 PCF, Windows FNT, BDF, PFR and Type 42. Note that this function knows nothing about the standard fonts installed on the user's system, thus you can't load them directly.

## Detailed Description

A FTP client.

[sf::Ftp](classsf_1_1Ftp.html "A FTP client.") is a very simple FTP client that allows you to communicate with a FTP server.

The FTP protocol allows you to manipulate a remote file system (list files, upload, download, create, remove, ...).

Using the FTP client consists of 4 parts:

* Connecting to the FTP server
* Logging in (either as a registered user or anonymously)
* Sending commands to the server
* Disconnecting (this part can be done implicitly by the destructor)

Every command returns a FTP response, which contains the status code as well as a message from the server. Some commands such as [getWorkingDirectory()](#a79c654fcdd0c81e68c4fa29af3b45e0c "Get the current working directory.") and [getDirectoryListing()](#a8f37258e461fcb9e2a0655e9df0be4a0 "Get the contents of the given directory.") return additional data, and use a class derived from [sf::Ftp::Response](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html "FTP response.") to provide this data. The most often used commands are directly provided as member functions, but it is also possible to use specific commands with the [sendCommand()](#a44e095103ecbce175a33eaf0820440ff "Send a command to the FTP server.") function.

Note that response statuses >= 1000 are not part of the FTP standard, they are generated by SFML when an internal error occurs.

All commands, especially upload and download, may take some time to complete. This is important to know if you don't want to block your application while the server is completing the task.

Usage example:

// Create a new FTP client

[sf::Ftp](classsf_1_1Ftp.html) ftp;

// Connect to the server

[sf::Ftp::Response](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html) response = ftp.[connect](#a4bf67543024815d11717ffe02cb8e1ef)("ftp://ftp.myserver.com");

if (response.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "Connected" << std::endl;

// Log in

response = ftp.[login](#a686262bc377584cd50e52e1576aa3a9b)("laurent", "dF6Zm89D");

if (response.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "Logged in" << std::endl;

// Print the working directory

[sf::Ftp::DirectoryResponse](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1DirectoryResponse.html) directory = ftp.[getWorkingDirectory](#a79c654fcdd0c81e68c4fa29af3b45e0c)();

if (directory.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "Working directory: " << directory.[getDirectory](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1DirectoryResponse.html#a407f96f0a473f52d9b12b5bf2505a5d5)() << std::endl;

// Create a new directory

response = ftp.[createDirectory](#a247b84c4b25da37804218c2b748c4787)("files");

if (response.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "Created new directory" << std::endl;

// Upload a file to this new directory

response = ftp.[upload](#adcc40761d3061e5b0d9d208eb5420f9b)("local-path/file.txt", "files", [sf::Ftp::TransferMode::Ascii](#a1cd6b89ad23253f6d97e6d4ca4d558cba76b8d0dcd02ccaf203c167ced6d7ef31));

if (response.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "File uploaded" << std::endl;

// Send specific commands (here: FEAT to list supported FTP features)

response = ftp.[sendCommand](#a44e095103ecbce175a33eaf0820440ff)("FEAT");

if (response.[isOk](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#a5102552955a2652c1a39e9046e617b36)())

std::cout << "Feature list:\n" << response.[getMessage](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#adc2890c93c9f8ee997b828fcbef82c97)() << std::endl;

// Disconnect from the server (optional)

ftp.[disconnect](#acf7459926f3391cd06bf84337ed6a0f4)();

## [◆](#a4bf67543024815d11717ffe02cb8e1ef)connect()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Response](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html) sf::Ftp::connect | ( | [IpAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html) | *server*, | |  |  | unsigned short | *port* = 21, | |  |  | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html) | *timeout* = [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0) ) | | nodiscard |

Connect to the specified FTP server.

The port has a default value of 21, which is the standard port used by the FTP protocol. You shouldn't use a different value, unless you really know what you do. This function tries to connect to the server so it may take a while to complete, especially if the server is not reachable. To avoid blocking your application for too long, you can use a timeout. The default value, [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0 "Predefined \"zero\" time value."), means that the system timeout will be used (which is usually pretty long).

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | server | Name or address of the FTP server to connect to |
    | port | Port used for the connection |
    | timeout | Maximum time to wait |

Returns
:   Server response to the request

See also
:   [disconnect](#acf7459926f3391cd06bf84337ed6a0f4 "Close the connection with the server.")

Send a command to the FTP server.

While the most often used commands are provided as member functions in the [sf::Ftp](classsf_1_1Ftp.html "A FTP client.") class, this method can be used to send any FTP command to the server. If the command requires one or more parameters, they can be specified in parameter. If the server returns information, you can extract it from the response using [Response::getMessage()](classsf_1_1Ftp_1_1Response.html#adc2890c93c9f8ee997b828fcbef82c97 "Get the full message contained in the response.").

:   Server response to the request

## Detailed Description

Base class for classes that require an OpenGL context.

This class is for internal use only, it must be the base of every class that requires a valid OpenGL context in order to work.

## Detailed Description

A HTTP client.

[sf::Http](classsf_1_1Http.html "A HTTP client.") is a very simple HTTP client that allows you to communicate with a web server.

You can retrieve web pages, send data to an interactive resource, download a remote file, etc. The HTTPS protocol is not supported.

The HTTP client is split into 3 classes:

* [sf::Http::Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html "HTTP request.")
* [sf::Http::Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html "HTTP response.")
* [sf::Http](classsf_1_1Http.html "A HTTP client.")

[sf::Http::Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html "HTTP request.") builds the request that will be sent to the server. A request is made of:

* a method (what you want to do)
* a target URI (usually the name of the web page or file)
* one or more header fields (options that you can pass to the server)
* an optional body (for POST requests)

[sf::Http::Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html "HTTP response.") parse the response from the web server and provides getters to read them. The response contains:

* a status code
* header fields (that may be answers to the ones that you requested)
* a body, which contains the contents of the requested resource

[sf::Http](classsf_1_1Http.html "A HTTP client.") provides a simple function, SendRequest, to send a [sf::Http::Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html "HTTP request.") and return the corresponding [sf::Http::Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html "HTTP response.") from the server.

Usage example:

// Create a new HTTP client

[sf::Http](classsf_1_1Http.html) http;

// We'll work on http://www.sfml-dev.org

http.[setHost](#a55121d543b61c41cf20b885a97b04e65)("http://www.sfml-dev.org");

// Prepare a request to get the 'features.php' page

[sf::Http::Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html) request("features.php");

// Send the request

[sf::Http::Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html) response = http.[sendRequest](#aaf09ebfb5e00dcc82e0d494d5c6a9e2a)(request);

// Check the status code and display the result

[sf::Http::Response::Status](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html#a663e071978e30fbbeb20ed045be874d8) status = response.[getStatus](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html#a4271651703764fd9a7d2c0315aff20de)();

if (status == [sf::Http::Response::Status::Ok](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html#a663e071978e30fbbeb20ed045be874d8aa60852f204ed8028c1c58808b746d115))

{

std::cout << response.[getBody](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html#ac59e2b11cae4b6232c737547a3ca9850)() << std::endl;

}

else

{

std::cout << "Error " << status << std::endl;

}

|  |  | unsigned short | *port* = 0 ) |

Construct the HTTP client with the target host.

This is equivalent to calling setHost(host, port). The port has a default value of 0, which means that the HTTP client will use the right port according to the protocol used (80 for HTTP). You should leave it like this unless you really need a port other than the standard one, or use an unknown protocol.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | host | Web server to connect to |
    | port | Port to use for connection |

## [◆](#aaf09ebfb5e00dcc82e0d494d5c6a9e2a)sendRequest()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html) sf::Http::sendRequest | ( | const [Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html) & | *request*, | |  |  | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html) | *timeout* = [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0) ) | | nodiscard |

Send a HTTP request and return the server's response.

You must have a valid host before sending a request (see setHost). Any missing mandatory header field in the request will be added with an appropriate value. Warning: this function waits for the server's response and may not return instantly; use a thread if you don't want to block your application, or use a timeout to limit the time to wait. A value of [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0 "Predefined \"zero\" time value.") means that the client will use the system default timeout (which is usually pretty long).

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | request | [Request](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Request.html "HTTP request.") to send |
    | timeout | Maximum time to wait |

Returns
:   Server's response

## [◆](#a55121d543b61c41cf20b885a97b04e65)setHost()

| void sf::Http::setHost | ( | const std::string & | *host*, |
|  |  | unsigned short | *port* = 0 ) |

Set the target host.

This function just stores the host address and port, it doesn't actually connect to it until you send a request. The port has a default value of 0, which means that the HTTP client will use the right port according to the protocol used (80 for HTTP). You should leave it like this unless you really need a port other than the standard one, or use an unknown protocol.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | host | Web server to connect to |
    | port | Port to use for connection |

The field is created if it doesn't exist. The name of the field is case-insensitive. By default, a request doesn't contain any field (but the mandatory fields are added later by the HTTP client when sending the request).

## Member Enumeration Documentation

## [◆](#a663e071978e30fbbeb20ed045be874d8)Status

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | enum class [sf::Http::Response::Status](#a663e071978e30fbbeb20ed045be874d8) | | strong |

Enumerate all the valid status codes for a response.

| Enumerator | |
| --- | --- |
| Ok | Most common code returned when operation was successful. |
| Created | The resource has successfully been created. |
| Accepted | The request has been accepted, but will be processed later by the server. |
| NoContent | The server didn't send any data in return. |
| ResetContent | The server informs the client that it should clear the view (form) that caused the request to be sent. |
| PartialContent | The server has sent a part of the resource, as a response to a partial GET request. |
| MultipleChoices | The requested page can be accessed from several locations. |
| MovedPermanently | The requested page has permanently moved to a new location. |
| MovedTemporarily | The requested page has temporarily moved to a new location. |
| NotModified | For conditional requests, means the requested page hasn't changed and doesn't need to be refreshed. |
| BadRequest | The server couldn't understand the request (syntax error) |
| Unauthorized | The requested page needs an authentication to be accessed. |
| Forbidden | The requested page cannot be accessed at all, even with authentication. |
| NotFound | The requested page doesn't exist. |
| RangeNotSatisfiable | The server can't satisfy the partial GET request (with a "Range" header field) |
| InternalServerError | The server encountered an unexpected error. |
| NotImplemented | The server doesn't implement a requested feature. |
| BadGateway | The gateway server has received an error from the source server. |
| ServiceNotAvailable | The server is temporarily unavailable (overloaded, in maintenance, ...) |
| GatewayTimeout | The gateway server couldn't receive a response from the source server. |
| VersionNotSupported | The server doesn't support the requested HTTP version. |
| InvalidResponse | [Response](classsf_1_1Http_1_1Response.html "HTTP response.") is not a valid HTTP one. |
| ConnectionFailed | Connection with server failed. |

| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | const std::string & sf::Http::Response::getBody | ( |  | ) | const | | nodiscard |

Get the body of the response.

The body of a response may contain:

* the requested page (for GET requests)
* a response from the server (for POST requests)
* nothing (for HEAD requests)
* an error message (in case of an error)

Returns
:   The response body

## Detailed Description

Class for loading, manipulating and saving images.

[sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html "Class for loading, manipulating and saving images.") is an abstraction to manipulate images as bi-dimensional arrays of pixels.

The class provides functions to load, read, write and save pixels, as well as many other useful functions.

[sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html "Class for loading, manipulating and saving images.") can handle a unique internal representation of pixels, which is RGBA 32 bits. This means that a pixel must be composed of 8 bit red, green, blue and alpha channels – just like a [sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html "Utility class for manipulating RGBA colors."). All the functions that return an array of pixels follow this rule, and all parameters that you pass to [sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html "Class for loading, manipulating and saving images.") functions (such as loadFromMemory) must use this representation as well.

A [sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html "Class for loading, manipulating and saving images.") can be copied, but it is a heavy resource and if possible you should always use [const] references to pass or return them to avoid useless copies.

Usage example:

// Load an image file from a file

const [sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html) background("background.jpg");

// Create a 20x20 image filled with black color

[sf::Image](classsf_1_1Image.html) image({20, 20}, [sf::Color::Black](classsf_1_1Color.html#a77c688197b981338f0b19dc58bd2facd));

// Copy background on image at position (10, 10)

if (!image.copy(background, {10, 10}))

return -1;

// Make the top-left pixel transparent

[sf::Color](classsf_1_1Color.html) color = image.getPixel({0, 0});

color.[a](classsf_1_1Color.html#a5a6825483a21a680a890379ed8a213a2) = 0;

image.setPixel({0, 0}, color);

// Save the image to a file

if (!image.saveToFile("result.png"))

return -1;

## [◆](#a5399551f13bd86c9f1b2d96ad52812ca)copy()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bool sf::Image::copy | ( | const [Image](classsf_1_1Image.html) & | *source*, | |  |  | [Vector2u](namespacesf.html#adc674b5f5c13a6734954a18e01a73b42) | *dest*, | |  |  | const [IntRect](namespacesf.html#add1cf75a734c8414680b0424145c30b1) & | *sourceRect* = {}, | |  |  | bool | *applyAlpha* = false ) | | nodiscard |

Copy pixels from another image onto this one.

This function does a slow pixel copy and should not be used intensively. It can be used to prepare a complex static image from several others, but if you need this kind of feature in real-time you'd better use [sf::RenderTexture](classsf_1_1RenderTexture.html "Target for off-screen 2D rendering into a texture.").

If sourceRect is empty, the whole image is copied. If applyAlpha is set to true, alpha blending is applied from the source pixels to the destination pixels using the **over** operator. If it is false, the source pixels are copied unchanged with their alpha value.

See <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_compositing> for details on the **over** operator.

Note that this function can fail if either image is invalid (i.e. zero-sized width or height), or if sourceRect is not within the boundaries of the source parameter, or if the destination area is out of the boundaries of this image.

On failure, the destination image is left unchanged.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | source | Source image to copy |
    | dest | Coordinates of the destination position |
    | sourceRect | Sub-rectangle of the source image to copy |
    | applyAlpha | Should the copy take into account the source transparency? |

Returns
:   true if the operation was successful, false otherwise

## [◆](#a85c60ac531015bc629737ea48a75cfda)getPixelsPtr()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | const std::uint8\_t \* sf::Image::getPixelsPtr | ( |  | ) | const | | nodiscard |

Get a read-only pointer to the array of pixels.

The returned value points to an array of RGBA pixels made of 8 bit integer components. The size of the array is width \* height \* 4 ([getSize()](#a85409951b05369813069ed64393391ce "Return the size (width and height) of the image.").x \* [getSize()](#a85409951b05369813069ed64393391ce "Return the size (width and height) of the image.").y \* 4). Warning: the returned pointer may become invalid if you modify the image, so you should never store it for too long. If the image is empty, a null pointer is returned.

Returns
:   Read-only pointer to the array of pixels

## Detailed Description

Provide read access to sound files.

This class decodes audio samples from a sound file.

It is used internally by higher-level classes such as [sf::SoundBuffer](classsf_1_1SoundBuffer.html "Storage for audio samples defining a sound.") and [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file."), but can also be useful if you want to process or analyze audio files without playing them, or if you want to implement your own version of [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file.") with more specific features.

Usage example:

// Open a sound file

[sf::InputSoundFile](classsf_1_1InputSoundFile.html) file("music.ogg");

// Print the sound attributes

std::cout << "duration: " << file.getDuration().asSeconds() << '\n'

<< "channels: " << file.getChannelCount() << '\n'

<< "sample rate: " << file.getSampleRate() << '\n'

<< "sample count: " << file.getSampleCount() << std::endl;

// Read and process batches of samples until the end of file is reached

std::array<std::int16\_t, 1024> samples;

std::uint64\_t count;

do

{

count = file.read(samples.data(), samples.size());

// process, analyze, play, convert, or whatever

// you want to do with the samples...

}

while (count > 0);

Construct a sound file from the disk for reading.

The supported audio formats are: WAV (PCM only), OGG/Vorbis, FLAC, MP3. The supported sample sizes for FLAC and WAV are 8, 16, 24 and 32 bit.

Because of minimp3\_ex limitation, for MP3 files with big (>16kb) APEv2 tag, it may not be properly removed, tag data will be treated as MP3 data and there is a low chance of garbage decoded at the end of file. See also: <https://github.com/lieff/minimp3>

## [◆](#afc98f7c941fbac7c2c0f697014b03b92)seek() [1/2]

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::InputSoundFile::seek | ( | std::uint64\_t | *sampleOffset* | ) |  |

Change the current read position to the given sample offset.

This function takes a sample offset to provide maximum precision. If you need to jump to a given time, use the other overload.

The sample offset takes the channels into account. If you have a time offset instead, you can easily find the corresponding sample offset with the following formula: timeInSeconds \* sampleRate \* channelCount If the given offset exceeds to total number of samples, this function jumps to the end of the sound file.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | sampleOffset | Index of the sample to jump to, relative to the beginning |

Change the current read position to the given time offset.

Using a time offset is handy but imprecise. If you need an accurate result, consider using the overload which takes a sample offset.

If the given time exceeds to total duration, this function jumps to the end of the sound file.

## Detailed Description

Abstract class for custom file input streams.

This class allows users to define their own file input sources from which SFML can load resources.

SFML resource classes like [sf::Texture](classsf_1_1Texture.html "Image living on the graphics card that can be used for drawing.") and [sf::SoundBuffer](classsf_1_1SoundBuffer.html "Storage for audio samples defining a sound.") provide loadFromFile and loadFromMemory functions, which read data from conventional sources. However, if you have data coming from a different source (over a network, embedded, encrypted, compressed, etc) you can derive your own class from [sf::InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.") and load SFML resources with their loadFromStream function.

Usage example:

// custom stream class that reads from inside a zip file

class ZipStream : public [sf::InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html)

{

public:

ZipStream(const std::string& archive);

[[nodiscard]] bool open(const std::filesystem::path& filename);

[[nodiscard]] std::optional<std::size\_t> [read](#a966518d3a4cba44ae5c28847865c487d)(void\* data, std::size\_t size);

[[nodiscard]] std::optional<std::size\_t> [seek](#ab53feb45aa824cc2117362ab79b38352)(std::size\_t position);

[[nodiscard]] std::optional<std::size\_t> [tell](#a03ec284866fd46ef2a3673e022f89895)();

std::optional<std::size\_t> [getSize](#a2d735fa531dd65747f743b09331ea7c8)();

private:

...

};

// now you can load textures...

ZipStream stream("resources.zip");

if (!stream.open("images/img.png"))

{

// Handle error...

}

const [sf::Texture](classsf_1_1Texture.html) texture(stream);

// musics...

[sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html) music;

ZipStream stream("resources.zip");

if (!stream.open("musics/msc.ogg"))

{

// Handle error...

}

if (!music.[openFromStream](classsf_1_1Music.html#a4e55d1910a26858b44778c26b237d673)(stream))

{

// Handle error...

}

// etc.

## Detailed Description

Encapsulate an IPv4 network address.

[sf::IpAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html "Encapsulate an IPv4 network address.") is a utility class for manipulating network addresses.

It provides a set a implicit constructors and conversion functions to easily build or transform an IP address from/to various representations.

Usage example:

auto a2 = [sf::IpAddress::resolve](#a4a78be2d092625c1216820037c2920c0)("127.0.0.1"); // the local host address

auto a3 = [sf::IpAddress::Broadcast](#aa93d1d57b65d243f2baf804b6035465c); // the broadcast address

[sf::IpAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html) a4(192, 168, 1, 56); // a local address

auto a5 = [sf::IpAddress::resolve](#a4a78be2d092625c1216820037c2920c0)("my\_computer"); // a local address created from a network name

auto a6 = [sf::IpAddress::resolve](#a4a78be2d092625c1216820037c2920c0)("89.54.1.169"); // a distant address

auto a7 = [sf::IpAddress::resolve](#a4a78be2d092625c1216820037c2920c0)("www.google.com"); // a distant address created from a network name

auto a8 = [sf::IpAddress::getLocalAddress](#a3076aa9ae952698930cb886d1ab0a1cc)(); // my address on the local network

auto a9 = [sf::IpAddress::getPublicAddress](#a361755453fb74920253e633c8523454b)(); // my address on the internet

Get the computer's local address.

The local address is the address of the computer from the LAN point of view, i.e. something like 192.168.1.56. It is meaningful only for communications over the local network. Unlike getPublicAddress, this function is fast and may be used safely anywhere.

Returns
:   Local IP address of the computer on success, std::nullopt otherwise

See also
:   [getPublicAddress](#a361755453fb74920253e633c8523454b "Get the computer's public address.")

## [◆](#a361755453fb74920253e633c8523454b)getPublicAddress()

Get the computer's public address.

The public address is the address of the computer from the internet point of view, i.e. something like 89.54.1.169. It is necessary for communications over the world wide web. The only way to get a public address is to ask it to a distant website; as a consequence, this function depends on both your network connection and the server, and may be very slow. You should use it as few as possible. Because this function depends on the network connection and on a distant server, you may use a time limit if you don't want your program to be possibly stuck waiting in case there is a problem; this limit is deactivated by default.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | timeout | Maximum time to wait |

Returns
:   Public IP address of the computer on success, std::nullopt otherwise

See also
:   [getLocalAddress](#a3076aa9ae952698930cb886d1ab0a1cc "Get the computer's local address.")

Get an integer representation of the address.

The returned number is the internal representation of the address, and should be used for optimization purposes only (like sending the address through a socket). The integer produced by this function can then be converted back to a [sf::IpAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html "Encapsulate an IPv4 network address.") with the proper constructor.

Returns

## Detailed Description

Implementation of input stream based on a memory chunk.

This class is a specialization of [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.") that reads from data in memory.

It wraps a memory chunk in the common [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.") interface and therefore allows to use generic classes or functions that accept such a stream, with content already loaded in memory.

In addition to the virtual functions inherited from [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams."), [MemoryInputStream](classsf_1_1MemoryInputStream.html "Implementation of input stream based on a memory chunk.") adds a function to specify the pointer and size of the data in memory.

SFML resource classes can usually be loaded directly from memory, so this class shouldn't be useful to you unless you create your own algorithms that operate on an [InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html "Abstract class for custom file input streams.").

Usage example:

void process([InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html)& stream);

[MemoryInputStream](#a3f2281ba28ef90b27573e1059119c20f) stream(thePtr, theSize);

process(stream);

[sf::InputStream](classsf_1_1InputStream.html)

Abstract class for custom file input streams.

## Detailed Description

Streamed music played from an audio file.

Musics are sounds that are streamed rather than completely loaded in memory.

This is especially useful for compressed musics that usually take hundreds of MB when they are uncompressed: by streaming it instead of loading it entirely, you avoid saturating the memory and have almost no loading delay. This implies that the underlying resource (file, stream or memory buffer) must remain valid for the lifetime of the [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file.") object.

Apart from that, a [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file.") has almost the same features as the [sf::SoundBuffer](classsf_1_1SoundBuffer.html "Storage for audio samples defining a sound.") / [sf::Sound](classsf_1_1Sound.html "Regular sound that can be played in the audio environment.") pair: you can play/pause/stop it, request its parameters (channels, sample rate), change the way it is played (pitch, volume, 3D position, ...), etc.

As a sound stream, a music is played in its own thread in order not to block the rest of the program. This means that you can leave the music alone after calling [play()](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#af05290eb2c6a316790fb18c5912a5dd6 "Start or resume playing the audio stream."), it will manage itself very well.

Usage example:

// Open a music from an audio file

[sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html) music("music.ogg");

// Change some parameters

music.setPosition({0, 1, 10}); // change its 3D position

music.setPitch(2); // increase the pitch

music.setVolume(50); // reduce the volume

music.setLooping(true); // make it loop

// Play it

music.play();

## [◆](#ab13ce12bd2ef4856511824557b07cce5)EffectProcessor

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| |  | | --- | | using [sf::SoundSource::EffectProcessor](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html#ab13ce12bd2ef4856511824557b07cce5) | | inherited |

**Initial value:**

std::function<

void(const float\* inputFrames, unsigned int& inputFrameCount, float\* outputFrames, unsigned int& outputFrameCount, unsigned int frameChannelCount)>

Callable that is provided with sound data for processing.

When the audio engine sources sound data from sound sources it will pass the data through an effects processor if one is set. The sound data will already be converted to the internal floating point format.

[Sound](classsf_1_1Sound.html "Regular sound that can be played in the audio environment.") data that is processed this way is provided in frames. Each frame contains 1 floating point sample per channel. If e.g. the data source provides stereo data, each frame will contain 2 floats.

The effects processor function takes 4 parameters:

* The input data frames, channels interleaved
* The number of input data frames available
* The buffer to write output data frames to, channels interleaved
* The number of output data frames that the output buffer can hold
* The channel count

The input and output frame counts are in/out parameters.

When this function is called, the input count will contain the number of frames available in the input buffer. The output count will contain the size of the output buffer i.e. the maximum number of frames that can be written to the output buffer.

Attempting to read more frames than the input frame count or write more frames than the output frame count will result in undefined behaviour.

It is important to note that the channel count of the audio engine currently sourcing data from this sound will always be provided in frameChannelCount. This can be different from the channel count of the sound source so make sure to size necessary processing buffers according to the engine channel count and not the sound source channel count.

When done processing the frames, the input and output frame counts must be updated to reflect the actual number of frames that were read from the input and written to the output.

The processing function should always try to process as much sound data as possible i.e. always try to fill the output buffer to the maximum. In certain situations for specific effects it can be possible that the input frame count and output frame count aren't equal. As long as the frame counts are updated accordingly this is perfectly valid.

If the audio engine determines that no audio data is available from the data source, the input data frames pointer is set to nullptr and the input frame count is set to 0. In this case it is up to the function to decide how to handle the situation. For specific effects e.g. Echo/Delay buffered data might still be able to be written to the output buffer even if there is no longer any input data.

An important thing to remember is that this function is directly called by the audio engine. Because the audio engine runs on an internal thread of its own, make sure access to shared data is synchronized appropriately.

Because this function is stored by the [SoundSource](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html "Base class defining a sound's properties.") object it will be able to be called as long as the [SoundSource](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html "Base class defining a sound's properties.") object hasn't yet been destroyed. Make sure that any data this function references outlives the [SoundSource](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html "Base class defining a sound's properties.") object otherwise use-after-free errors will occur.

| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sf::Music::Music | ( | const std::filesystem::path & | *filename* | ) |  | | explicit |

Construct a music from an audio file.

This function doesn't start playing the music (call [play()](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#af05290eb2c6a316790fb18c5912a5dd6 "Start or resume playing the audio stream.") to do so). See the documentation of [sf::InputSoundFile](classsf_1_1InputSoundFile.html "Provide read access to sound files.") for the list of supported formats.

Warning
:   Since the music is not loaded at once but rather streamed continuously, the file must remain accessible until the [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file.") object loads a new music or is destroyed.

## [◆](#acc7af0cebb8ca0ca4ab8edccd46499ab)Music() [3/5]

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sf::Music::Music | ( | const void \* | *data*, |
|  |  | std::size\_t | *sizeInBytes* ) |

Construct a music from an audio file in memory.

This function doesn't start playing the music (call [play()](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#af05290eb2c6a316790fb18c5912a5dd6 "Start or resume playing the audio stream.") to do so). See the documentation of [sf::InputSoundFile](classsf_1_1InputSoundFile.html "Provide read access to sound files.") for the list of supported formats.

Warning
:   Since the music is not loaded at once but rather streamed continuously, the *data* buffer must remain accessible until the [sf::Music](classsf_1_1Music.html "Streamed music played from an audio file.") object loads a new music or is destroyed. That is, you can't deallocate the buffer right after calling this function.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | data | Pointer to the file data in memory |
    | sizeInBytes | Size of the data to load, in bytes |

Exceptions
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | [sf::Exception](classsf_1_1Exception.html "Library-specific exception type.") | if loading was unsuccessful |

See also
:   [openFromFile](#a9493f462e07423d891f117a8b4c613fe "Open a music from an audio file."), [openFromStream](#a4e55d1910a26858b44778c26b237d673 "Open a music from an audio file in a custom stream.")

This function must be called by derived classes as soon as they know the audio settings of the stream to play. Any attempt to manipulate the stream ([play()](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#af05290eb2c6a316790fb18c5912a5dd6 "Start or resume playing the audio stream."), ...) before calling this function will fail. It can be called multiple times if the settings of the audio stream change, but only when the stream is stopped.

## [◆](#a1edba64c835fd76ba474965dee216aaf)onLoop()

Change the current playing position in the stream source to the loop offset.

This is called by the underlying [SoundStream](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html "Abstract base class for streamed audio sources.") whenever it needs us to reset the seek position for a loop. We then determine whether we are looping on a loop point or the end-of-file, perform the seek, and return the new position.

Returns
:   The seek position after looping (or std::nullopt if there's no loop)

Reimplemented from [sf::SoundStream](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#ac7c8b90227522b48f357ac856d6e0853).

See the documentation of [sf::InputSoundFile](classsf_1_1InputSoundFile.html "Provide read access to sound files.") for the list of supported formats.

Start or resume playing the audio stream.

This function starts the stream if it was stopped, resumes it if it was paused, and restarts it from the beginning if it was already playing. This function uses its own thread so that it doesn't block the rest of the program while the stream is played.

:   [pause](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#a2285cedcbcb5f3c97828c664934dc0de "Pause the audio stream."), [stop](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#a781fe51135fdc5679fe22a5665110143 "Stop playing the audio stream.")

Set the attenuation factor of the sound.

The attenuation is a multiplicative factor which makes the sound more or less loud according to its distance from the listener. An attenuation of 0 will produce a non-attenuated sound, i.e. its volume will always be the same whether it is heard from near or from far. On the other hand, an attenuation value such as 100 will make the sound fade out very quickly as it gets further from the listener. The default value of the attenuation is 1.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | attenuation | New attenuation factor of the sound |

See also
:   [getAttenuation](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html#a8ad7dafb4f1b4afbc638cebe24f48cc9 "Get the attenuation factor of the sound."), [setMinDistance](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html#a75bbc2c34addc8b25a14edb908508afe "Set the minimum distance of the sound.")

## [◆](#ae7b339f0a957dfad045f3f28083a015e)setLoopPoints()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::Music::setLoopPoints | ( | [TimeSpan](#a8f92f34d1714edb7178ba2a8a5a845e8) | *timePoints* | ) |  |

Sets the beginning and duration of the sound's looping sequence using [sf::Time](classsf_1_1Time.html "Represents a time value.")

[setLoopPoints()](#ae7b339f0a957dfad045f3f28083a015e "Sets the beginning and duration of the sound's looping sequence using sf::Time") allows for specifying the beginning offset and the duration of the loop such that, when the music is enabled for looping, it will seamlessly seek to the beginning whenever it encounters the end of the duration. Valid ranges for timePoints.offset and timePoints.length are [0, Dur) and (0, Dur-offset] respectively, where Dur is the value returned by [getDuration()](#a288ef6f552a136b0e56952dcada3d672 "Get the total duration of the music."). Note that the EOF "loop point" from the end to the beginning of the stream is still honored, in case the caller seeks to a point after the end of the loop range. This function can be safely called at any point after a stream is opened, and will be applied to a playing sound without affecting the current playing offset.

Warning
:   Setting the loop points while the stream's status is Paused will set its status to Stopped. The playing offset will be unaffected.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | timePoints | The definition of the loop. Can be any time points within the sound's length |

See also
:   [getLoopPoints](#aae3451cad5c16ee6a6e124e62ed61361 "Get the positions of the of the sound's looping sequence.")

This function stops the stream if it was playing or paused, and does nothing if it was already stopped. It also resets the playing position (unlike [pause()](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#a2285cedcbcb5f3c97828c664934dc0de "Pause the audio stream.")).

See also
:   [play](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#af05290eb2c6a316790fb18c5912a5dd6 "Start or resume playing the audio stream."), [pause](classsf_1_1SoundStream.html#a2285cedcbcb5f3c97828c664934dc0de "Pause the audio stream.")

Implements [sf::SoundSource](classsf_1_1SoundSource.html#a06501a25b12376befcc7ee1ed4865fda).

## Detailed Description

Provide write access to sound files.

This class encodes audio samples to a sound file.

It is used internally by higher-level classes such as [sf::SoundBuffer](classsf_1_1SoundBuffer.html "Storage for audio samples defining a sound."), but can also be useful if you want to create audio files from custom data sources, like generated audio samples.

Usage example:

// Create a sound file, ogg/vorbis format, 44100 Hz, stereo

[sf::OutputSoundFile](classsf_1_1OutputSoundFile.html) file("music.ogg", 44100, 2, {[sf::SoundChannel::FrontLeft](group__audio.html#gga9800c7f3d5e7a9c9310f707b2c995ff3a3a86c1ecef856c6360b14ee920abd2d4), [sf::SoundChannel::FrontRight](group__audio.html#gga9800c7f3d5e7a9c9310f707b2c995ff3a17a1a1897fa234ffd995f32ff31c4075)});

while (...)

{

// Read or generate audio samples from your custom source

std::vector<std::int16\_t> samples = ...;

// Write them to the file

file.write(samples.data(), samples.size());

}

## Detailed Description

Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network.

Packets provide a safe and easy way to serialize data, in order to send it over the network using sockets ([sf::TcpSocket](classsf_1_1TcpSocket.html "Specialized socket using the TCP protocol."), [sf::UdpSocket](classsf_1_1UdpSocket.html "Specialized socket using the UDP protocol.")).

Packets solve 2 fundamental problems that arise when transferring data over the network:

* data is interpreted correctly according to the endianness
* the bounds of the packet are preserved (one send == one receive)

The [sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html "Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network.") class provides both input and output modes. It is designed to follow the behavior of standard C++ streams, using operators >> and << to extract and insert data.

It is recommended to use only fixed-size types (like std::int32\_t, etc.), to avoid possible differences between the sender and the receiver. Indeed, the native C++ types may have different sizes on two platforms and your data may be corrupted if that happens.

Usage example:

std::uint32\_t x = 24;

std::string s = "hello";

double d = 5.89;

// Group the variables to send into a packet

[sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html) packet;

packet << x << s << d;

// Send it over the network (socket is a valid sf::TcpSocket)

socket.send(packet);

-----------------------------------------------------------------

// Receive the packet at the other end

[sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html) packet;

socket.receive(packet);

// Extract the variables contained in the packet

std::uint32\_t x;

std::string s;

double d;

if (packet >> x >> s >> d)

{

// Data extracted successfully...

}

[sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html)

Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network.

**Definition** [Packet.hpp:49](Packet_8hpp_source.html#l00048)

Packets have built-in operator>> and << overloads for standard types:

* bool
* fixed-size integer types (int[8|16|32]\_t, uint[8|16|32]\_t)
* floating point numbers (float, double)
* string types (char\*, wchar\_t\*, std::string, std::wstring, [sf::String](classsf_1_1String.html "Utility string class that automatically handles conversions between types and encodings."))

Like standard streams, it is also possible to define your own overloads of operators >> and << in order to handle your custom types.

struct MyStruct

{

float number{};

std::int8\_t integer{};

std::string str;

};

sf::Packet& [operator <<](#ae02c874e0aac18a0497fca982a8f9083)(sf::Packet& packet, const MyStruct& m)

{

return packet << m.number << m.integer << m.str;

}

sf::Packet& [operator >>](#a8b6403506fec6b69f033278de33c8145)(sf::Packet& packet, MyStruct& m)

{

return packet >> m.number >> m.integer >> m.str;

}

[sf::Packet::operator>>](#a8b6403506fec6b69f033278de33c8145)

Packet & operator>>(bool &data)

Overload of operator>> to read data from the packet.

[sf::Packet::operator<<](#ae02c874e0aac18a0497fca982a8f9083)

Packet & operator<<(bool data)

Overload of operator<< to write data into the packet.

Packets also provide an extra feature that allows to apply custom transformations to the data before it is sent, and after it is received. This is typically used to handle automatic compression or encryption of the data. This is achieved by inheriting from [sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html "Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network."), and overriding the onSend and onReceive functions.

Here is an example:

class ZipPacket : public [sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html)

{

const void\* [onSend](#af0003506bcb290407dcf5fe7f13a887d)(std::size\_t& size) override

{

const void\* srcData = [getData](#a998b70df024bee4792e2ecdc915ae46e)();

std::size\_t srcSize = [getDataSize](#a0fae6eccf2ca704fc5099cd90a9f56f7)();

return MySuperZipFunction(srcData, srcSize, &size);

}

void [onReceive](#ab71a31ef0f1d5d856de6f9fc75434128)(const void\* data, std::size\_t size) override

{

std::size\_t dstSize;

const void\* dstData = MySuperUnzipFunction(data, size, &dstSize);

[append](#a7dd6e429b87520008326c4d71f1cf011)(dstData, dstSize);

}

};

// Use like regular packets:

ZipPacket packet;

packet << x << s << d;

...

## [◆](#ab71a31ef0f1d5d856de6f9fc75434128)onReceive()

| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | virtual void sf::Packet::onReceive | ( | const void \* | *data*, | |  |  | std::size\_t | *size* ) | | protectedvirtual |

Called after the packet is received over the network.

This function can be defined by derived classes to transform the data after it is received; this can be used for decompression, decryption, etc. The function receives a pointer to the received data, and must fill the packet with the transformed bytes. The default implementation fills the packet directly without transforming the data.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | data | Pointer to the received bytes |
    | size | Number of bytes |

See also
:   [onSend](#af0003506bcb290407dcf5fe7f13a887d "Called before the packet is sent over the network.")

Called before the packet is sent over the network.

This function can be defined by derived classes to transform the data before it is sent; this can be used for compression, encryption, etc. The function must return a pointer to the modified data, as well as the number of bytes pointed. The default implementation provides the packet's data without transforming it.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | size | Variable to fill with the size of data to send |

Returns
:   Pointer to the array of bytes to send

## [◆](#a8863ff08b73f728a341c775758abbfb4)operator bool()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | sf::Packet::operator bool | ( |  | ) | const | | explicit |

Test the validity of the packet, for reading.

This operator allows to test the packet as a boolean variable, to check if a reading operation was successful.

A packet will be in an invalid state if it has no more data to read.

This behavior is the same as standard C++ streams.

Usage example:

float x;

packet >> x;

if (packet)

{

// ok, x was extracted successfully

}

// -- or --

float x;

if (packet >> x)

{

// ok, x was extracted successfully

}

Returns
:   true if last data extraction from packet was successful

See also
:   [endOfPacket](#a61e354fa670da053907c14b738839560 "Tell if the reading position has reached the end of the packet.")
