## Detailed Description

Specialized socket using the UDP protocol.

A UDP socket is a connectionless socket.

Instead of connecting once to a remote host, like TCP sockets, it can send to and receive from any host at any time.

It is a datagram protocol: bounded blocks of data (datagrams) are transferred over the network rather than a continuous stream of data (TCP). Therefore, one call to send will always match one call to receive (if the datagram is not lost), with the same data that was sent.

The UDP protocol is lightweight but unreliable. Unreliable means that datagrams may be duplicated, be lost or arrive reordered. However, if a datagram arrives, its data is guaranteed to be valid.

UDP is generally used for real-time communication (audio or video streaming, real-time games, etc.) where speed is crucial and lost data doesn't matter much.

Sending and receiving data can use either the low-level or the high-level functions. The low-level functions process a raw sequence of bytes, whereas the high-level interface uses packets (see [sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html "Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network.")), which are easier to use and provide more safety regarding the data that is exchanged. You can look at the [sf::Packet](classsf_1_1Packet.html "Utility class to build blocks of data to transfer over the network.") class to get more details about how they work.

It is important to note that [UdpSocket](classsf_1_1UdpSocket.html "Specialized socket using the UDP protocol.") is unable to send datagrams bigger than MaxDatagramSize. In this case, it returns an error and doesn't send anything. This applies to both raw data and packets. Indeed, even packets are unable to split and recompose data, due to the unreliability of the protocol (dropped, mixed or duplicated datagrams may lead to a big mess when trying to recompose a packet).

If the socket is bound to a port, it is automatically unbound from it when the socket is destroyed. However, you can unbind the socket explicitly with the Unbind function if necessary, to stop receiving messages or make the port available for other sockets.

Usage example:

// ----- The client -----

// Create a socket and bind it to the port 55001

[sf::UdpSocket](classsf_1_1UdpSocket.html) socket;

socket.[bind](#a1bd7b273613665d5ef4dcecf5767ed75)(55001);

// Send a message to 192.168.1.50 on port 55002

std::string message = "Hi, I am " + [sf::IpAddress::getLocalAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html#a3076aa9ae952698930cb886d1ab0a1cc)().toString();

socket.[send](#a78b46f2a2345284339367bb44bab78cf)(message.c\_str(), message.size() + 1, "192.168.1.50", 55002);

// Receive an answer (most likely from 192.168.1.50, but could be anyone else)

std::array<char, 1024> buffer;

std::size\_t received = 0;

std::optional<sf::IpAddress> sender;

unsigned short port;

if (socket.[receive](#a3fdcfaf926ae4de72ab59573b408169d)(buffer.data(), buffer.size(), received, sender, port) == [sf::Socket::Status::Done](classsf_1_1Socket.html#a51bf0fd51057b98a10fbb866246176dcaf92965e2c8a7afb3c1b9a5c09a263636))

std::cout << sender->toString() << " said: " << buffer.data() << std::endl;

// ----- The server -----

// Create a socket and bind it to the port 55002

[sf::UdpSocket](classsf_1_1UdpSocket.html) socket;

socket.[bind](#a1bd7b273613665d5ef4dcecf5767ed75)(55002);

// Receive a message from anyone

std::array<char, 1024> buffer;

std::size\_t received = 0;

std::optional<sf::IpAddress> sender;

unsigned short port;

if (socket.[receive](#a3fdcfaf926ae4de72ab59573b408169d)(buffer.data(), buffer.size(), received, sender, port) == [sf::Socket::Status::Done](classsf_1_1Socket.html#a51bf0fd51057b98a10fbb866246176dcaf92965e2c8a7afb3c1b9a5c09a263636))

std::cout << sender->toString() << " said: " << buffer.data() << std::endl;

// Send an answer

std::string message = "Welcome " + sender.toString();

socket.[send](#a78b46f2a2345284339367bb44bab78cf)(message.c\_str(), message.size() + 1, sender, port);

## [◆](#a1bd7b273613665d5ef4dcecf5767ed75)bind()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Status](classsf_1_1Socket.html#a51bf0fd51057b98a10fbb866246176dc) sf::UdpSocket::bind | ( | unsigned short | *port*, | |  |  | [IpAddress](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html) | *address* = [IpAddress::Any](classsf_1_1IpAddress.html#a3dbc10b0dc6804cc69e29342f7406907) ) | | nodiscard |

Bind the socket to a specific port.

Binding the socket to a port is necessary for being able to receive data on that port.

When providing [sf::Socket::AnyPort](classsf_1_1Socket.html#a16dfada3e5ba1773ac434bc70510221f "Some special values used by sockets.") as port, the listener will request an available port from the system. The chosen port can be retrieved by calling [getLocalPort()](#a5c03644b3da34bb763bce93e758c938e "Get the port to which the socket is bound locally.").

Since the socket can only be bound to a single port at any given moment, if it is already bound when this function is called, it will be unbound from the previous port before being bound to the new one.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | port | Port to bind the socket to |
    | address | Address of the interface to bind to |

Returns
:   [Status](classsf_1_1Socket.html#a51bf0fd51057b98a10fbb866246176dc "Status codes that may be returned by socket functions.") code

See also
:   [unbind](#a2c4abb8102a1bd31f51fcfe7f15427a3 "Unbind the socket from the local port to which it is bound."), [getLocalPort](#a5c03644b3da34bb763bce93e758c938e "Get the port to which the socket is bound locally.")

## [◆](#a165fc1423e281ea2714c70303d3a9782)setBlocking()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::Socket::setBlocking | ( | bool | *blocking* | ) |  | | inherited |

Set the blocking state of the socket.

In blocking mode, calls will not return until they have completed their task. For example, a call to Receive in blocking mode won't return until some data was actually received. In non-blocking mode, calls will always return immediately, using the return code to signal whether there was data available or not. By default, all sockets are blocking.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | blocking | true to set the socket as blocking, false for non-blocking |

See also
:   [isBlocking](classsf_1_1Socket.html#ab1ceca9ac114b8baeeda3b34a0aca468 "Tell whether the socket is in blocking or non-blocking mode.")

## [◆](#a2c4abb8102a1bd31f51fcfe7f15427a3)unbind()

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::UdpSocket::unbind | ( |  | ) |  |

Unbind the socket from the local port to which it is bound.

The port that the socket was previously bound to is immediately made available to the operating system after this function is called. This means that a subsequent call to [bind()](#a1bd7b273613665d5ef4dcecf5767ed75 "Bind the socket to a specific port.") will be able to re-bind the port if no other process has done so in the mean time. If the socket is not bound to a port, this function has no effect.

See also
:   [bind](#a1bd7b273613665d5ef4dcecf5767ed75 "Bind the socket to a specific port.")

## Detailed Description

template<unsigned int N>  
class sf::Utf< N >

Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.

[sf::Utf](classsf_1_1Utf.html "Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.") is a low-level, generic interface for counting, iterating, encoding and decoding Unicode characters and strings. It is able to handle ANSI, wide, latin-1, UTF-8, UTF-16 and UTF-32 encodings.

[sf::Utf](classsf_1_1Utf.html "Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.")<X> functions are all static, these classes are not meant to be instantiated. All the functions are template, so that you can use any character / string type for a given encoding.

It has 3 specializations:

* [sf::Utf](classsf_1_1Utf.html "Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.")<8> (with [sf::Utf8](namespacesf.html#af8632a98df098830707aa50ab82029b8) type alias)
* [sf::Utf](classsf_1_1Utf.html "Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.")<16> (with [sf::Utf16](namespacesf.html#a99b0ac57adecd5594ce6dda56bfe6f70) type alias)
* [sf::Utf](classsf_1_1Utf.html "Utility class providing generic functions for UTF conversions.")<32> (with [sf::Utf32](namespacesf.html#a3f2bd4822b2d2563557e3d1d400f6cb8) type alias)

## Detailed Description

template<typename T>  
class sf::Vector2< T >

Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.

[sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.") is a simple class that defines a mathematical vector with two coordinates (x and y).

It can be used to represent anything that has two dimensions: a size, a point, a velocity, a scale, etc.

The API provides basic arithmetic (addition, subtraction, scale), as well as more advanced geometric operations, such as dot/cross products, length and angle computations, projections, rotations, etc.

The template parameter T is the type of the coordinates. It can be any type that supports arithmetic operations (+, -, /, \*) and comparisons (==, !=), for example int or float. Note that some operations are only meaningful for vectors where T is a floating point type (e.g. float or double), often because results cannot be represented accurately with integers. The method documentation mentions "(floating-point)" in those cases.

You generally don't have to care about the templated form ([sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")<T>), the most common specializations have special type aliases:

* [sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")<float> is [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)
* [sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")<int> is [sf::Vector2i](namespacesf.html#af0ffe1b157a56931ee3a9a1a771a827a)
* [sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")<unsigned int> is [sf::Vector2u](namespacesf.html#adc674b5f5c13a6734954a18e01a73b42)

The [sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.") class has a simple interface, its x and y members can be accessed directly (there are no accessors like setX(), getX()).

Usage example:

[sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d) v(16.5f, 24.f);

v.x = 18.2f;

float [y](#a420f2481b015f4eb929c75f2af564299) = v.y;

[sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d) w = v \* 5.f;

[sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d) u;

u = v + w;

float s = v.[dot](#aee222bf5c5cf5f88e33aa013e25a7b37)(w);

bool different = (v != u);

|  |  | [Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html) | *phi* ) |

Construct the vector from polar coordinates ***(floating-point)***

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | r | Length of vector (can be negative) |
    | phi | [Angle](classsf_1_1Angle.html "Represents an angle value.") from X axis |

Note that this constructor is lossy: calling [length()](#a0f99a27817ae528e249e7a8053217e5f "Length of the vector (floating-point).") and [angle()](#ae147c7f7d85347e1adc2e1a66ad87498 "Signed angle from +X or (1,0) vector (floating-point).") may return values different to those provided in this constructor.

In particular, these transforms can be applied:

* Vector2(r, phi) == [Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")(-r, phi + 180\_deg)
* Vector2(r, phi) == [Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")(r, phi + n \* 360\_deg)

Component-wise multiplication of \*this and rhs.

Computes (lhs.x\*rhs.x, lhs.y\*rhs.y).

Scaling is the most common use case for component-wise multiplication/division. This operation is also known as the Hadamard or Schur product.

Returns a perpendicular vector.

Returns \*this rotated by +90 degrees; (x,y) becomes (-y,x). For example, the vector (1,0) is transformed to (0,1).

In SFML's default coordinate system with +X right and +Y down, this amounts to a clockwise rotation.

## Detailed Description

template<typename T>  
class sf::Vector3< T >

Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.

[sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.") is a simple class that defines a mathematical vector with three coordinates (x, y and z).

It can be used to represent anything that has three dimensions: a size, a point, a velocity, etc.

The template parameter T is the type of the coordinates. It can be any type that supports arithmetic operations (+, -, /, \*) and comparisons (==, !=), for example int or float. Note that some operations are only meaningful for vectors where T is a floating point type (e.g. float or double), often because results cannot be represented accurately with integers. The method documentation mentions "(floating-point)" in those cases.

You generally don't have to care about the templated form ([sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.")<T>), the most common specializations have special type aliases:

* [sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.")<float> is [sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0)
* [sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.")<int> is [sf::Vector3i](namespacesf.html#ac128b1a250ca87839ef1dd0416b45961)

The [sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.") class has a small and simple interface, its x, y and z members can be accessed directly (there are no accessors like setX(), getX()).

Usage example:

[sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0) v(16.5f, 24.f, -3.2f);

v.x = 18.2f;

float [y](#a6590d50ccb862c5efc5512e974e9b794) = v.y;

[sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0) w = v \* 5.f;

[sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0) u;

u = v + w;

float s = v.[dot](#a3415efbdf1c7d57bea45157e5031d493)(w);

[sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0) t = v.cross(w);

bool different = (v != u);

Component-wise division of \*this and rhs.

Computes (lhs.x/rhs.x, lhs.y/rhs.y, lhs.z/rhs.z).

Scaling is the most common use case for component-wise multiplication/division.

Precondition
:   Neither component of rhs is zero.

Component-wise multiplication of \*this and rhs.

Computes (lhs.x\*rhs.x, lhs.y\*rhs.y, lhs.z\*rhs.z).

Scaling is the most common use case for component-wise multiplication/division. This operation is also known as the Hadamard or Schur product.

## Detailed Description

Set of one or more 2D primitives.

[sf::VertexArray](classsf_1_1VertexArray.html "Set of one or more 2D primitives.") is a very simple wrapper around a dynamic array of vertices and a primitives type.

It inherits [sf::Drawable](classsf_1_1Drawable.html "Abstract base class for objects that can be drawn to a render target."), but unlike other drawables it is not transformable.

Example:

[sf::VertexArray](classsf_1_1VertexArray.html) lines([sf::PrimitiveType::LineStrip](group__graphics.html#gga5ee56ac1339984909610713096283b1bae7f9e73b8edd21f420a63b3ace5768a2), 4);

lines[0].position = [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(10, 0);

lines[1].position = [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(20, 0);

lines[2].position = [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(30, 5);

lines[3].position = [sf::Vector2f](namespacesf.html#af14b40e82368dd601a7ef8037214804d)(40, 2);

window.draw(lines);

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::VertexArray::clear | ( |  | ) |  |

Clear the vertex array.

This function removes all the vertices from the array. It doesn't deallocate the corresponding memory, so that adding new vertices after clearing doesn't involve reallocating all the memory.

| void sf::VertexArray::resize | ( | std::size\_t | *vertexCount* | ) |  |

Resize the vertex array.

If vertexCount is greater than the current size, the previous vertices are kept and new (default-constructed) vertices are added. If vertexCount is less than the current size, existing vertices are removed from the array.

Set the type of primitives to draw.

This function defines how the vertices must be interpreted when it's time to draw them:

* As points
* As lines
* As triangles The default primitive type is [sf::PrimitiveType::Points](group__graphics.html#gga5ee56ac1339984909610713096283b1ba75dd5f1160a3f02b6fae89c54361a1b3 "List of individual points.").

## Detailed Description

[Vertex](structsf_1_1Vertex.html "Point with color and texture coordinates.") buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives.

[sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html "Vertex buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives.") is a simple wrapper around a dynamic buffer of vertices and a primitives type.

Unlike [sf::VertexArray](classsf_1_1VertexArray.html "Set of one or more 2D primitives."), the vertex data is stored in graphics memory.

In situations where a large amount of vertex data would have to be transferred from system memory to graphics memory every frame, using [sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html "Vertex buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives.") can help. By using a [sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html "Vertex buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives."), data that has not been changed between frames does not have to be re-transferred from system to graphics memory as would be the case with [sf::VertexArray](classsf_1_1VertexArray.html "Set of one or more 2D primitives."). If data transfer is a bottleneck, this can lead to performance gains.

Using [sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html "Vertex buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives."), the user also has the ability to only modify a portion of the buffer in graphics memory. This way, a large buffer can be allocated at the start of the application and only the applicable portions of it need to be updated during the course of the application. This allows the user to take full control of data transfers between system and graphics memory if they need to.

In special cases, the user can make use of multiple threads to update vertex data in multiple distinct regions of the buffer simultaneously. This might make sense when e.g. the position of multiple objects has to be recalculated very frequently. The computation load can be spread across multiple threads as long as there are no other data dependencies.

Simultaneous updates to the vertex buffer are not guaranteed to be carried out by the driver in any specific order. Updating the same region of the buffer from multiple threads will not cause undefined behavior, however the final state of the buffer will be unpredictable.

Simultaneous updates of distinct non-overlapping regions of the buffer are also not guaranteed to complete in a specific order. However, in this case the user can make sure to synchronize the writer threads at well-defined points in their code. The driver will make sure that all pending data transfers complete before the vertex buffer is sourced by the rendering pipeline.

It inherits [sf::Drawable](classsf_1_1Drawable.html "Abstract base class for objects that can be drawn to a render target."), but unlike other drawables it is not transformable.

Example:

std::array<sf::Vertex, 15> vertices;

...

sf::VertexBuffer triangles([sf::PrimitiveType::Triangles](group__graphics.html#gga5ee56ac1339984909610713096283b1ba7ca66fdfaad3eb33fc65d7490178f856));

triangles.create(vertices.size());

triangles.update(vertices.data());

...

window.draw(triangles);

[sf::PrimitiveType::Triangles](group__graphics.html#gga5ee56ac1339984909610713096283b1ba7ca66fdfaad3eb33fc65d7490178f856)

@ Triangles

List of individual triangles.

[Usage](#a3a531528684e63ecb45edd51282f5cb7 "Usage specifiers.") specifiers.

If data is going to be updated once or more every frame, set the usage to Stream. If data is going to be set once and used for a long time without being modified, set the usage to Static. For everything else Dynamic should be a good compromise.

| Enumerator | |
| --- | --- |
| Stream | Constantly changing data. |
| Dynamic | Occasionally changing data. |
| Static | Rarely changing data. |

Bind a vertex buffer for rendering.

This function is not part of the graphics API, it mustn't be used when drawing SFML entities. It must be used only if you mix [sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html "Vertex buffer storage for one or more 2D primitives.") with OpenGL code.

[sf::VertexBuffer](classsf_1_1VertexBuffer.html) vb1, vb2;

...

sf::VertexBuffer::bind(&vb1);

// draw OpenGL stuff that use vb1...

[sf::VertexBuffer::bind](#a1c623e9701b43125e4b3661bc0d0b65b)(&vb2);

// draw OpenGL stuff that use vb2...

[sf::VertexBuffer::bind](#a1c623e9701b43125e4b3661bc0d0b65b)(nullptr);

// draw OpenGL stuff that use no vertex buffer...

Set the usage specifier of this vertex buffer.

This function provides a hint about how this vertex buffer is going to be used in terms of data update frequency.

After changing the usage specifier, the vertex buffer has to be updated with new data for the usage specifier to take effect.

The default usage type is [sf::VertexBuffer::Usage::Stream](#a3a531528684e63ecb45edd51282f5cb7aeae835e83c0494a376229f254f7d3392 "Constantly changing data.").

## [◆](#ae6c8649a64861507010d21e77fbd53fa)update() [2/3]

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bool sf::VertexBuffer::update | ( | const [Vertex](structsf_1_1Vertex.html) \* | *vertices*, | |  |  | std::size\_t | *vertexCount*, | |  |  | unsigned int | *offset* ) | | nodiscard |

Update a part of the buffer from an array of vertices.

offset is specified as the number of vertices to skip from the beginning of the buffer.

If offset is 0 and vertexCount is equal to the size of the currently created buffer, its whole contents are replaced.

If offset is 0 and vertexCount is greater than the size of the currently created buffer, a new buffer is created containing the vertex data.

If offset is 0 and vertexCount is less than the size of the currently created buffer, only the corresponding region is updated.

If offset is not 0 and offset + vertexCount is greater than the size of the currently created buffer, the update fails.

No additional check is performed on the size of the vertex array. Passing invalid arguments will lead to undefined behavior.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | vertices | Array of vertices to copy to the buffer |
    | vertexCount | Number of vertices to copy |
    | offset | Offset in the buffer to copy to |

Returns
:   true if the update was successful

## Detailed Description

[VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html "VideoMode defines a video mode (size, bpp)") defines a video mode (size, bpp)

A video mode is defined by a width and a height (in pixels) and a depth (in bits per pixel).

Video modes are used to setup windows ([sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.")) at creation time.

The main usage of video modes is for fullscreen mode: indeed you must use one of the valid video modes allowed by the OS (which are defined by what the monitor and the graphics card support), otherwise your window creation will just fail.

[sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html "VideoMode defines a video mode (size, bpp)") provides a static function for retrieving the list of all the video modes supported by the system: [getFullscreenModes()](#a0f99e67ef2b51fbdc335d9991232609e "Retrieve all the video modes supported in fullscreen mode.").

A custom video mode can also be checked directly for fullscreen compatibility with its [isValid()](#ad5e04c044b0925523c75ecb173d2129a "Tell whether or not the video mode is valid.") function.

Additionally, [sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html "VideoMode defines a video mode (size, bpp)") provides a static function to get the mode currently used by the desktop: [getDesktopMode()](#ac1be160a4342e6eafb2cb0e8c9b18d44 "Get the current desktop video mode."). This allows to build windows with the same size or pixel depth as the current resolution.

Usage example:

// Display the list of all the video modes available for fullscreen

std::vector<sf::VideoMode> modes = [sf::VideoMode::getFullscreenModes](#a0f99e67ef2b51fbdc335d9991232609e)();

for (std::size\_t i = 0; i < modes.size(); ++i)

{

[sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html) mode = modes[i];

std::cout << "Mode #" << i << ": "

<< mode.[size](#afa7b60723adc1c39e43075a157d35d98).[x](classsf_1_1Vector2.html#a1e6ad77fa155f3753bfb92699bd28141) << "x" << mode.[size](#afa7b60723adc1c39e43075a157d35d98).[y](classsf_1_1Vector2.html#a420f2481b015f4eb929c75f2af564299) << " - "

<< mode.[bitsPerPixel](#aa080f1ef96a1008d58b1920eceb189df) << " bpp" << std::endl;

}

// Create a window with the same pixel depth as the desktop

[sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html) desktop = [sf::VideoMode::getDesktopMode](#ac1be160a4342e6eafb2cb0e8c9b18d44)();

window.create([sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html)({1024, 768}, desktop.[bitsPerPixel](#aa080f1ef96a1008d58b1920eceb189df)), "SFML window");

## [◆](#a0f99e67ef2b51fbdc335d9991232609e)getFullscreenModes()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | const std::vector< [VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html) > & sf::VideoMode::getFullscreenModes | ( |  | ) |  | | staticnodiscard |

Retrieve all the video modes supported in fullscreen mode.

When creating a fullscreen window, the video mode is restricted to be compatible with what the graphics driver and monitor support. This function returns the complete list of all video modes that can be used in fullscreen mode. The returned array is sorted from best to worst, so that the first element will always give the best mode (higher width, height and bits-per-pixel).

Returns
:   Array containing all the supported fullscreen modes

## Detailed Description

2D camera that defines what region is shown on screen

[sf::View](classsf_1_1View.html "2D camera that defines what region is shown on screen") defines a camera in the 2D scene.

This is a very powerful concept: you can scroll, rotate or zoom the entire scene without altering the way that your drawable objects are drawn.

A view is composed of a source rectangle, which defines what part of the 2D scene is shown, and a target viewport, which defines where the contents of the source rectangle will be displayed on the render target (window or texture).

The viewport allows to map the scene to a custom part of the render target, and can be used for split-screen or for displaying a minimap, for example. If the source rectangle doesn't have the same size as the viewport, its contents will be stretched to fit in.

The scissor rectangle allows for specifying regions of the render target to which modifications can be made by draw and clear operations. Only pixels that are within the region will be able to be modified. Pixels outside of the region will not be modified by draw or clear operations.

Certain effects can be created by either using the viewport or scissor rectangle. While the results appear identical, there can be times where one method should be preferred over the other. Viewport transformations are applied during the vertex processing stage of the graphics pipeline, before the primitives are rasterized into fragments for fragment processing. Since viewport processing has to be performed and cannot be disabled, effects that are performed using the viewport transform are basically free performance-wise. Scissor testing is performed in the per-sample processing stage of the graphics pipeline, after fragment processing has been performed. Because per-sample processing is performed at the last stage of the pipeline, fragments that are discarded at this stage will cause the highest waste of GPU resources compared to any method that would have discarded vertices or fragments earlier in the pipeline. There are situations in which scissor testing has to be used to control whether fragments are discarded or not. An example of such a situation is when performing the viewport transform on vertices is necessary but a subset of the generated fragments should not have an effect on the stencil buffer or blend with the color buffer.

## [◆](#a51029b20359f9889f4e0ad8c8254abc9)setScissor()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::View::setScissor | ( | const [FloatRect](namespacesf.html#a701020eb396e62ba560619e68c689a38) & | *scissor* | ) |  |

Set the target scissor rectangle.

The scissor rectangle, expressed as a factor (between 0 and 1) of the [RenderTarget](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html "Base class for all render targets (window, texture, ...)"), specifies the region of the [RenderTarget](classsf_1_1RenderTarget.html "Base class for all render targets (window, texture, ...)") whose pixels are able to be modified by draw or clear operations. Any pixels which lie outside of the scissor rectangle will not be modified by draw or clear operations. For example, a scissor rectangle which only allows modifications to the right side of the target would be defined with view.setScissor([sf::FloatRect](namespacesf.html#a701020eb396e62ba560619e68c689a38)({0.5f, 0.f}, {0.5f, 1.f})). By default, a view has a scissor rectangle which allows modifications to the entire target. This is equivalent to disabling the scissor test entirely. Passing the default scissor rectangle to this function will also disable scissor testing.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | scissor | New scissor rectangle |

See also
:   [getScissor](#a46ea8dd5eff1148b0bd54e4270a7a0ce "Get the scissor rectangle of the view.")

## [◆](#a4a72a360a5792fbe4e99cd6feaf7726e)zoom()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::View::zoom | ( | float | *factor* | ) |  |

Resize the view rectangle relative to its current size.

Resizing the view simulates a zoom, as the zone displayed on screen grows or shrinks. *factor* is a multiplier:

* 1 keeps the size unchanged
* > 1 makes the view bigger (objects appear smaller)
* < 1 makes the view smaller (objects appear bigger)

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | factor | Zoom factor to apply |

See also
:   [setSize](#a49ad66679cd7a461917eaee587020354 "Set the size of the view."), [move](#a5df7c26db6583f0a59bc0522b27348f1 "Move the view relative to its current position."), [rotate](#a23c24a1ec48c3e50aba2307adaddaf93 "Rotate the view relative to its current orientation.")

## Detailed Description

[Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.

[sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") is the main class of the [Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") module.

It defines an OS window that is able to receive an OpenGL rendering.

A [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") can create its own new window, or be embedded into an already existing control using the create(handle) function. This can be useful for embedding an OpenGL rendering area into a view which is part of a bigger GUI with existing windows, controls, etc. It can also serve as embedding an OpenGL rendering area into a window created by another (probably richer) GUI library like Qt or wxWidgets.

The [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") class provides a simple interface for manipulating the window: move, resize, show/hide, control mouse cursor, etc. It also provides event handling through its [pollEvent()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.") and [waitEvent()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it.") functions.

Note that OpenGL experts can pass their own parameters (anti-aliasing level, bits for the depth and stencil buffers, etc.) to the OpenGL context attached to the window, with the [sf::ContextSettings](structsf_1_1ContextSettings.html "Structure defining the settings of the OpenGL context attached to a window.") structure which is passed as an optional argument when creating the window.

On dual-graphics systems consisting of a low-power integrated GPU and a powerful discrete GPU, the driver picks which GPU will run an SFML application. In order to inform the driver that an SFML application can benefit from being run on the more powerful discrete GPU, #SFML\_DEFINE\_DISCRETE\_GPU\_PREFERENCE can be placed in a source file that is compiled and linked into the final application. The macro should be placed outside of any scopes in the global namespace.

Usage example:

// Declare and create a new window

[sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html) window([sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html)({800, 600}), "SFML window");

// Limit the framerate to 60 frames per second (this step is optional)

window.[setFramerateLimit](#af4322d315baf93405bf0d5087ad5e784)(60);

// The main loop - ends as soon as the window is closed

while (window.[isOpen](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#aa43559822564ef958dc664a90c57cba0)())

{

// Event processing

while (const std::optional event = window.[pollEvent](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35)())

{

// Request for closing the window

if (event->is<[sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)>())

window.[close](#ab1d808a3682db8d113d67354bcbd717d)();

}

// Activate the window for OpenGL rendering

window.[setActive](#aaab549da64cedf74fa6f1ae7a3cc79e0)();

// OpenGL drawing commands go here...

// End the current frame and display its contents on screen

window.[display](#adabf839cb103ac96cfc82f781638772a)();

}

Construct a new window.

This constructor creates the window with the size and pixel depth defined in mode. An optional style can be passed to customize the look and behavior of the window (borders, title bar, resizable, closable, ...). An optional state can be provided. If state is [State::Fullscreen](group__window.html#gga504e2cd8fc6a852463f8d049db1151e5a0829ea6734059d66e6bf87096b215dc1 "Fullscreen window."), then mode must be a valid video mode.

The last parameter is an optional structure specifying advanced OpenGL context settings such as anti-aliasing, depth-buffer bits, etc.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | mode | Video mode to use (defines the width, height and depth of the rendering area of the window) |
    | title | Title of the window |
    | style | Window style, a bitwise OR combination of [sf::Style](namespacesf_1_1Style.html) enumerators |
    | state | Window state |
    | settings | Additional settings for the underlying OpenGL context |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::Window::close | ( |  | ) |  | | overridevirtual |

Close the window and destroy all the attached resources.

After calling this function, the [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") instance remains valid and you can call [create()](#ae77f112046c240b477963326e2363e18 "Create (or recreate) the window.") to recreate the window. All other functions such as [pollEvent()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.") or [display()](#adabf839cb103ac96cfc82f781638772a "Display on screen what has been rendered to the window so far.") will still work (i.e. you don't have to test [isOpen()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#aa43559822564ef958dc664a90c57cba0 "Tell whether or not the window is open.") every time), and will have no effect on closed windows.

Reimplemented from [sf::WindowBase](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a9a5ea0ba0ab584dbd11bbfea233b457f).

## [◆](#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9)handleEvents()

template<typename... Handlers>

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::WindowBase::handleEvents | ( | Handlers &&... | *handlers* | ) |  | | inherited |

Handle all pending events.

This function is not blocking: if there's no pending event then it will return without calling any of the handlers.

This function can take a variadic list of event handlers that each take a concrete event type as a single parameter. The event handlers can be any kind of callable object that has an operator() defined for a specific event type. Additionally a generic callable can also be provided that will be invoked for every event type. If both types of callables are provided, the callables taking concrete event types will be preferred over the generic callable by overload resolution. Generic callables can be used to customize handler dispatching based on the deduced type of the event and other information available at compile time.

Examples of callables:

* Lambda expressions: [&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html "Key pressed event subtype.")) { ... }
* Free functions: void handler(const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html "Key pressed event subtype.")&) { ... }

// Only provide handlers for concrete event types

window.handleEvents(

[&](const [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)&) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)& keyPress) { /\* handle event \*/ }

);

[sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)

Key pressed event subtype.

**Definition** [Event.hpp:97](Event_8hpp_source.html#l00096)

// Provide a generic event handler

window.handleEvents(

[&](const auto& event)

{

if constexpr (std::is\_same\_v<std::decay\_t<decltype(event)>, [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)>)

{

// Handle Closed

handleClosed();

}

else if constexpr (std::is\_same\_v<std::decay\_t<decltype(event)>, [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)>)

{

// Handle KeyPressed

handleKeyPressed(event);

}

else

{

// Handle non-KeyPressed

handleOtherEvents(event);

}

}

);

// Provide handlers for concrete types and fall back to generic handler

window.handleEvents(

[&](const [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)&) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)& keyPress) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const auto& event) { /\* handle all other events \*/ }

);

Calling member functions is supported through lambda expressions.

// Provide a generic event handler

window.handleEvents(

[this](const auto& event) { handle(event); }

);

| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::optional< [Event](classsf_1_1Event.html) > sf::WindowBase::pollEvent | ( |  | ) |  | | nodiscardinherited |

Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.

This function is not blocking: if there's no pending event then it will return a std::nullopt. Note that more than one event may be present in the event queue, thus you should always call this function in a loop to make sure that you process every pending event.

while (const std::optional event = window.pollEvent())

{

// process event...

}

Returns
:   The event, otherwise std::nullopt if no events are pending

See also
:   [waitEvent](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it."), [handleEvents](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9 "Handle all pending events.")

## [◆](#a448770d2372d8df0a1ad6b1c7cce3c89)requestFocus()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | void sf::WindowBase::requestFocus | ( |  | ) |  | | inherited |

Request the current window to be made the active foreground window.

At any given time, only one window may have the input focus to receive input events such as keystrokes or mouse events. If a window requests focus, it only hints to the operating system, that it would like to be focused. The operating system is free to deny the request. This is not to be confused with [setActive()](#aaab549da64cedf74fa6f1ae7a3cc79e0 "Activate or deactivate the window as the current target for OpenGL rendering.").

See also
:   [hasFocus](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#ad87bd19e979c426cb819ccde8c95232e "Check whether the window has the input focus.")

| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bool sf::Window::setActive | ( | bool | *active* = true | ) | const | | nodiscard |

Activate or deactivate the window as the current target for OpenGL rendering.

A window is active only on the current thread, if you want to make it active on another thread you have to deactivate it on the previous thread first if it was active. Only one window can be active on a thread at a time, thus the window previously active (if any) automatically gets deactivated. This is not to be confused with [requestFocus()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a448770d2372d8df0a1ad6b1c7cce3c89 "Request the current window to be made the active foreground window.").

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | active | true to activate, false to deactivate |

Returns
:   true if operation was successful, false otherwise

## [◆](#af4322d315baf93405bf0d5087ad5e784)setFramerateLimit()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::Window::setFramerateLimit | ( | unsigned int | *limit* | ) |  |

Limit the framerate to a maximum fixed frequency.

If a limit is set, the window will use a small delay after each call to [display()](#adabf839cb103ac96cfc82f781638772a "Display on screen what has been rendered to the window so far.") to ensure that the current frame lasted long enough to match the framerate limit. SFML will try to match the given limit as much as it can, but since it internally uses [sf::sleep](group__system.html#gab8c0d1f966b4e5110fd370b662d8c11b "Make the current thread sleep for a given duration."), whose precision depends on the underlying OS, the results may be a little imprecise as well (for example, you can get 65 FPS when requesting 60).

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | limit | Framerate limit, in frames per seconds (use 0 to disable limit) |

## [◆](#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7)waitEvent()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::optional< [Event](classsf_1_1Event.html) > sf::WindowBase::waitEvent | ( | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html) | *timeout* = [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0) | ) |  | | nodiscardinherited |

Wait for an event and return it.

This function is blocking: if there's no pending event then it will wait until an event is received or until the provided timeout elapses. Only if an error or a timeout occurs the returned event will be std::nullopt. This function is typically used when you have a thread that is dedicated to events handling: you want to make this thread sleep as long as no new event is received.

while (const std::optional event = window.waitEvent())

{

// process event...

}

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | timeout | Maximum time to wait ([Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0 "Predefined \"zero\" time value.") for infinite) |

Returns
:   The event, otherwise std::nullopt on timeout or if window was closed

See also
:   [pollEvent](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it."), [handleEvents](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9 "Handle all pending events.")

## Detailed Description

[Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") that serves as a base for other windows.

[sf::WindowBase](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html "Window that serves as a base for other windows.") serves as the base class for all Windows.

A [sf::WindowBase](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html "Window that serves as a base for other windows.") can create its own new window, or be embedded into an already existing control using the create(handle) function.

The [sf::WindowBase](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html "Window that serves as a base for other windows.") class provides a simple interface for manipulating the window: move, resize, show/hide, control mouse cursor, etc. It also provides event handling through its [pollEvent()](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.") and [waitEvent()](#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it.") functions.

Usage example:

// Declare and create a new window

[sf::WindowBase](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html) window([sf::VideoMode](classsf_1_1VideoMode.html)({800, 600}), "SFML window");

// The main loop - ends as soon as the window is closed

while (window.[isOpen](#aa43559822564ef958dc664a90c57cba0)())

{

// Event processing

while (const std::optional event = window.[pollEvent](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35)())

{

// Request for closing the window

if (event->is<[sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)>())

window.[close](#a9a5ea0ba0ab584dbd11bbfea233b457f)();

}

// Do things with the window here...

}

Construct a new window.

This constructor creates the window with the size and pixel depth defined in mode. An optional style can be passed to customize the look and behavior of the window (borders, title bar, resizable, closable, ...). An optional state can be provided. If state is [State::Fullscreen](group__window.html#gga504e2cd8fc6a852463f8d049db1151e5a0829ea6734059d66e6bf87096b215dc1 "Fullscreen window."), then mode must be a valid video mode.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | mode | Video mode to use (defines the width, height and depth of the rendering area of the window) |
    | title | Title of the window |
    | style | Window style, a bitwise OR combination of [sf::Style](namespacesf_1_1Style.html) enumerators |
    | state | Window state |

## [◆](#a9a5ea0ba0ab584dbd11bbfea233b457f)close()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | virtual void sf::WindowBase::close | ( |  | ) |  | | virtual |

Close the window and destroy all the attached resources.

After calling this function, the [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") instance remains valid and you can call [create()](#a612f5918f3cb042fcf1189fed24b91d4 "Create (or recreate) the window.") to recreate the window. All other functions such as [pollEvent()](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.") or display() will still work (i.e. you don't have to test [isOpen()](#aa43559822564ef958dc664a90c57cba0 "Tell whether or not the window is open.") every time), and will have no effect on closed windows.

Reimplemented in [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html#ab1d808a3682db8d113d67354bcbd717d).

## [◆](#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9)handleEvents()

template<typename... Handlers>

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::WindowBase::handleEvents | ( | Handlers &&... | *handlers* | ) |  |

Handle all pending events.

This function is not blocking: if there's no pending event then it will return without calling any of the handlers.

This function can take a variadic list of event handlers that each take a concrete event type as a single parameter. The event handlers can be any kind of callable object that has an operator() defined for a specific event type. Additionally a generic callable can also be provided that will be invoked for every event type. If both types of callables are provided, the callables taking concrete event types will be preferred over the generic callable by overload resolution. Generic callables can be used to customize handler dispatching based on the deduced type of the event and other information available at compile time.

Examples of callables:

* Lambda expressions: [&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html "Key pressed event subtype.")) { ... }
* Free functions: void handler(const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html "Key pressed event subtype.")&) { ... }

// Only provide handlers for concrete event types

window.handleEvents(

[&](const [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)&) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)& keyPress) { /\* handle event \*/ }

);

// Provide handlers for concrete types and fall back to generic handler

window.handleEvents(

[&](const [sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)&) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const [sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)& keyPress) { /\* handle event \*/ },

[&](const auto& event) { /\* handle all other events \*/ }

);

Calling member functions is supported through lambda expressions.

// Provide a generic event handler

window.handleEvents(

[this](const auto& event) { handle(event); }

);

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | handlers | A variadic list of callables that take a specific event as their only parameter |

See also
:   [waitEvent](#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it."), [pollEvent](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.")

## [◆](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35)pollEvent()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::optional< [Event](classsf_1_1Event.html) > sf::WindowBase::pollEvent | ( |  | ) |  | | nodiscard |

Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it.

This function is not blocking: if there's no pending event then it will return a std::nullopt. Note that more than one event may be present in the event queue, thus you should always call this function in a loop to make sure that you process every pending event.

while (const std::optional event = window.pollEvent())

{

// process event...

}

Returns
:   The event, otherwise std::nullopt if no events are pending

See also
:   [waitEvent](#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7 "Wait for an event and return it."), [handleEvents](#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9 "Handle all pending events.")

## [◆](#a448770d2372d8df0a1ad6b1c7cce3c89)requestFocus()

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::WindowBase::requestFocus | ( |  | ) |  |

Request the current window to be made the active foreground window.

At any given time, only one window may have the input focus to receive input events such as keystrokes or mouse events. If a window requests focus, it only hints to the operating system, that it would like to be focused. The operating system is free to deny the request. This is not to be confused with setActive().

See also
:   [hasFocus](#ad87bd19e979c426cb819ccde8c95232e "Check whether the window has the input focus.")

## [◆](#ab5975f6f6a06ecd6c18fa0f62cd1edf7)waitEvent()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::optional< [Event](classsf_1_1Event.html) > sf::WindowBase::waitEvent | ( | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html) | *timeout* = [Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0) | ) |  | | nodiscard |

Wait for an event and return it.

This function is blocking: if there's no pending event then it will wait until an event is received or until the provided timeout elapses. Only if an error or a timeout occurs the returned event will be std::nullopt. This function is typically used when you have a thread that is dedicated to events handling: you want to make this thread sleep as long as no new event is received.

while (const std::optional event = window.waitEvent())

{

// process event...

}

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | timeout | Maximum time to wait ([Time::Zero](classsf_1_1Time.html#a8db127b632fa8da21550e7282af11fa0 "Predefined \"zero\" time value.") for infinite) |

Returns
:   The event, otherwise std::nullopt on timeout or if window was closed

See also
:   [pollEvent](#a6090926b477e9d0a83854b94b9e1fd35 "Pop the next event from the front of the FIFO event queue, if any, and return it."), [handleEvents](#a0f3289445ce7103e85c56571c4bc0de9 "Handle all pending events.")

| |  | | --- | | enum class [sf::SoundChannel](#ga9800c7f3d5e7a9c9310f707b2c995ff3) | | strong |

Types of sound channels that can be read/written from sound buffers/files.

In multi-channel audio, each sound channel can be assigned a position. The position of the channel is used to determine where to place a sound when it is spatialized. Assigning an incorrect sound channel will result in multi-channel audio being positioned incorrectly when using spatialization.

## Detailed Description

Base module of SFML, defining various utilities.

It provides vector classes, Unicode strings and conversion functions, threads and mutexes, timing classes.

## Function Documentation

## [◆](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b)err()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::ostream & sf::err | ( |  | ) |  | | nodiscard |

Standard stream used by SFML to output warnings and errors.

By default, [sf::err()](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b "Standard stream used by SFML to output warnings and errors.") outputs to the same location as std::cerr, (-> the stderr descriptor) which is the console if there's one available.

It is a standard std::ostream instance, so it supports all the insertion operations defined by the STL (operator<<, manipulators, etc.).

[sf::err()](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b "Standard stream used by SFML to output warnings and errors.") can be redirected to write to another output, independently of std::cerr, by using the rdbuf() function provided by the std::ostream class.

Example:

// Redirect to a file

std::ofstream file("sfml-log.txt");

std::streambuf\* previous = [sf::err](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b)().rdbuf(file.rdbuf());

// Redirect to nothing

[sf::err](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b)().rdbuf(nullptr);

// Restore the original output

[sf::err](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b)().rdbuf(previous);

[sf::err](#ga885486205a724571d140a7c8a0e3626b)

std::ostream & err()

Standard stream used by SFML to output warnings and errors.

Returns
:   Reference to std::ostream representing the SFML error stream

Return a pointer to the Android native activity.

You shouldn't have to use this function, unless you want to implement very specific details, that SFML doesn't support, or to use a workaround for a known issue.

Returns
:   Pointer to Android native activity structure

Platform Limitation
:   **This is only available on Android** and to use it, you'll have to specifically include [SFML/System/NativeActivity.hpp](NativeActivity_8hpp.html) in your code.

## [◆](#gab8c0d1f966b4e5110fd370b662d8c11b)sleep()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::sleep | ( | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html) | *duration* | ) |  |

Make the current thread sleep for a given duration.

[sf::sleep](#gab8c0d1f966b4e5110fd370b662d8c11b "Make the current thread sleep for a given duration.") is the best way to block a program or one of its threads, as it doesn't consume any CPU power. Compared to the standard std::this\_thread::sleep\_for function, this one provides more accurate sleeping time thanks to some platform-specific tweaks.

[sf::sleep](#gab8c0d1f966b4e5110fd370b662d8c11b "Make the current thread sleep for a given duration.") only guarantees millisecond precision. Sleeping for a duration less than 1 millisecond is prone to result in the actual sleep duration being less than what is requested.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | duration | [Time](classsf_1_1Time.html "Represents a time value.") to sleep |

| --- |
| using [sf::WindowHandle](#ga9858f04701033cd01859037d8dafd289) = "platform-specific" |

Low-level window handle type, specific to each platform.

| Platform | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `HWND` |
| Linux/FreeBSD | `Window` |
| macOS | either `NSWindow*` or `NSView*`, disguised as `void*` |
| iOS | `UIWindow*` |
| Android | `ANativeWindow*` |

macOS Specification

On macOS, a [sf::Window](classsf_1_1Window.html "Window that serves as a target for OpenGL rendering.") can be created either from an existing `NSWindow*` or an `NSView*`. When the window is created from a window, SFML will use its content view as the OpenGL area. [sf::Window::getNativeHandle()](classsf_1_1WindowBase.html#af360bb48167c6db4d13e47d23d9c35da "Get the OS-specific handle of the window.") will return the handle that was used to create the window, which is a `NSWindow*` by default.

| |  | | --- | | enum class [sf::StencilComparison](#a5a1510ae19d01cf19178b8f3ef92a2a1) | | strong |

Enumeration of the stencil test comparisons that can be performed.

The comparisons are mapped directly to their OpenGL equivalents, specified by glStencilFunc().

| Enumerator | |
| --- | --- |
| Never | The stencil test never passes. |
| Less | The stencil test passes if the new value is less than the value in the stencil buffer. |
| LessEqual | The stencil test passes if the new value is less than or equal to the value in the stencil buffer. |
| Greater | The stencil test passes if the new value is greater than the value in the stencil buffer. |
| GreaterEqual | The stencil test passes if the new value is greater than or equal to the value in the stencil buffer. |
| Equal | The stencil test passes if the new value is strictly equal to the value in the stencil buffer. |
| NotEqual | The stencil test passes if the new value is strictly unequal to the value in the stencil buffer. |
| Always | The stencil test always passes. |

Enumeration of the stencil buffer update operations.

The update operations are mapped directly to their OpenGL equivalents, specified by glStencilOp().

| Enumerator | |
| --- | --- |
| Keep | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is not modified. |
| Zero | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is set to zero. |
| Replace | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is set to the new value. |
| Increment | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is incremented and if required clamped. |
| Decrement | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is decremented and if required clamped. |
| Invert | If the stencil test passes, the value in the stencil buffer is bitwise inverted. |

## Detailed Description

Give access to the system clipboard.

[sf::Clipboard](namespacesf_1_1Clipboard.html "Give access to the system clipboard.") provides an interface for getting and setting the contents of the system clipboard.

It is important to note that due to limitations on some operating systems, setting the clipboard contents is only guaranteed to work if there is currently an open window for which events are being handled.

Usage example:

// get the clipboard content as a string

[sf::String](classsf_1_1String.html) string = [sf::Clipboard::getString](#a5ffa170c4fa8674b90725936412b79aa)();

// or use it in the event loop

while (const std::optional event = window.pollEvent())

{

if (event->is<[sf::Event::Closed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1Closed.html)>())

window.close();

if (const auto\* keyPressed = event->getIf<[sf::Event::KeyPressed](structsf_1_1Event_1_1KeyPressed.html)>())

{

// Using Ctrl + V to paste a string into SFML

if (keyPressed->control && keyPressed->code == [sf::Keyboard::Key::V](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a5206560a306a2e085a437fd258eb57ce))

string = [sf::Clipboard::getString](#a5ffa170c4fa8674b90725936412b79aa)();

// Using Ctrl + C to copy a string out of SFML

if (keyPressed->control && keyPressed->code == [sf::Keyboard::Key::C](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a0d61f8370cad1d412f80b84d143e1257))

[sf::Clipboard::setString](#a5ab898e1e6498c0312f24ff50aa2ccb3)("Hello World!");

}

}

## Detailed Description

Namespace with GLSL types.

The [sf::Glsl](namespacesf_1_1Glsl.html "Namespace with GLSL types.") namespace contains types that match their equivalents in GLSL, the OpenGL shading language. These types are exclusively used by the [sf::Shader](classsf_1_1Shader.html "Shader class (vertex, geometry and fragment)") class.

Types that already exist in SFML, such as [sf::Vector2](classsf_1_1Vector2.html "Class template for manipulating 2-dimensional vectors.")<T> and [sf::Vector3](classsf_1_1Vector3.html "Utility template class for manipulating 3-dimensional vectors.")<T>, are reused as type aliases, so you can use the types in this namespace as well as the original ones. Others are newly defined, such as [Glsl::Vec4](#abf169ad4f8b5405d6b2f37ecd9d28cbd "4D float vector (vec4 in GLSL)") or [Glsl::Mat3](#a207da683a577343ae0633aed1b1fa12f "3x3 float matrix (mat3 in GLSL)"). Their actual type is an implementation detail and should not be used.

All vector types support a default constructor that initializes every component to zero, in addition to a constructor with one parameter for each component. The components are stored in member variables called x, y, z, and w.

All matrix types support a constructor with a float\* parameter that points to a float array of the appropriate size (that is, 9 in a 3x3 matrix, 16 in a 4x4 matrix). Furthermore, they can be converted from [sf::Transform](classsf_1_1Transform.html "3x3 transform matrix") objects.

See also
:   [sf::Shader](classsf_1_1Shader.html "Shader class (vertex, geometry and fragment)")

{

1, 0, 0,

0, 1, 0,

x, y, 1

};

[sf::Glsl::Mat3](#a207da683a577343ae0633aed1b1fa12f) matrix(array);

## Detailed Description

Give access to the real-time state of the joysticks.

[sf::Joystick](namespacesf_1_1Joystick.html "Give access to the real-time state of the joysticks.") provides an interface to the state of the joysticks.

Each joystick is identified by an index that is passed to the functions in this namespace.

This namespace allows users to query the state of joysticks at any time and directly, without having to deal with a window and its events. Compared to the JoystickMoved, JoystickButtonPressed and JoystickButtonReleased events, [sf::Joystick](namespacesf_1_1Joystick.html "Give access to the real-time state of the joysticks.") can retrieve the state of axes and buttons of joysticks at any time (you don't need to store and update a boolean on your side in order to know if a button is pressed or released), and you always get the real state of joysticks, even if they are moved, pressed or released when your window is out of focus and no event is triggered.

SFML supports:

* 8 joysticks ([sf::Joystick::Count](#a459467658a2542bdf56903229e431068 "Constants related to joysticks capabilities."))
* 32 buttons per joystick ([sf::Joystick::ButtonCount](#a650d9cc7232acb2b3a32b92166ed0c77 "Maximum number of supported buttons."))
* 8 axes per joystick ([sf::Joystick::AxisCount](#a0de8fc66336c6764151d88af5b42d2bb "Maximum number of supported axes."))

Unlike the keyboard or mouse, the state of joysticks is sometimes not directly available (depending on the OS), therefore an [update()](#a924f051f4c3d66a980918fda6b0ff787 "Update the states of all joysticks.") function must be called in order to update the current state of joysticks. When you have a window with event handling, this is done automatically, you don't need to call anything. But if you have no window, or if you want to check joysticks state before creating one, you must call [sf::Joystick::update](#a924f051f4c3d66a980918fda6b0ff787 "Update the states of all joysticks.") explicitly.

Usage example:

// Is joystick #0 connected?

bool connected = [sf::Joystick::isConnected](#a8e312bfb03954efa373326dbda3f911d)(0);

// How many buttons does joystick #0 support?

unsigned int buttons = [sf::Joystick::getButtonCount](#a31e0644c53d26e46618e5b6acdf2f5f2)(0);

// Does joystick #0 define a X axis?

bool hasX = [sf::Joystick::hasAxis](#afa7b0a9e74d47067670f37362a655a76)(0, [sf::Joystick::Axis::X](#a48db337092c2e263774f94de6d50baa7a02129bb861061d1a052c592e2dc6b383));

// Is button #2 pressed on joystick #0?

bool pressed = [sf::Joystick::isButtonPressed](#af45b5a3883b80a54ecb9c5a5f1fc78b5)(0, 2);

// What's the current position of the Y axis on joystick #0?

float position = [sf::Joystick::getAxisPosition](#a572af0673215579abf76a52665341338)(0, [sf::Joystick::Axis::Y](#a48db337092c2e263774f94de6d50baa7a57cec4137b614c87cb4e24a3d003a3e0));

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| void sf::Joystick::update | ( |  | ) |  |

Update the states of all joysticks.

This function is used internally by SFML, so you normally don't have to call it explicitly. However, you may need to call it if you have no window yet (or no window at all): in this case the joystick states are not updated automatically.

## Detailed Description

Give access to the real-time state of the keyboard.

[sf::Keyboard](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html "Give access to the real-time state of the keyboard.") provides an interface to the state of the keyboard.

This namespace allows users to query the keyboard state at any time and directly, without having to deal with a window and its events. Compared to the KeyPressed and KeyReleased events, [sf::Keyboard](namespacesf_1_1Keyboard.html "Give access to the real-time state of the keyboard.") can retrieve the state of a key at any time (you don't need to store and update a boolean on your side in order to know if a key is pressed or released), and you always get the real state of the keyboard, even if keys are pressed or released when your window is out of focus and no event is triggered.

Usage example:

if ([sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed](#ae081baf14e88668e1b0831ce85aa07f5)([sf::Keyboard::Key::Left](#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a945d5e233cf7d6240f6b783b36a374ff)))

{

// move left...

}

else if ([sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed](#ae081baf14e88668e1b0831ce85aa07f5)([sf::Keyboard::Key::Right](#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a92b09c7c48c520c3c55e497875da437c)))

{

// move right...

}

else if ([sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed](#ae081baf14e88668e1b0831ce85aa07f5)([sf::Keyboard::Key::Escape](#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a013ec032d3460d4be4431c6ab1f8f224)))

{

// quit...

}

else if ([sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed](#ae081baf14e88668e1b0831ce85aa07f5)([sf::Keyboard::Scan::Grave](#aed978288ff367518d29cfe0c9e3b295faed24ff8971b1fa43a1efbb386618ce35)))

{

// open in-game command line (if it's not already open)

}

## [◆](#a7b9e69295a65cdf4d6084f841ff6ef42)getDescription()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [String](classsf_1_1String.html) sf::Keyboard::getDescription | ( | [Scancode](#aed978288ff367518d29cfe0c9e3b295f) | *code* | ) |  | | nodiscard |

Provide a string representation for a given scancode.

The returned string is a short, non-technical description of the key represented with the given scancode. Most effectively used in user interfaces, as the description for the key takes the users keyboard layout into consideration.

Warning
:   The result is OS-dependent: for example, [sf::Keyboard::Scan::LSystem](#aed978288ff367518d29cfe0c9e3b295fafc2ae39512975c67ebe724fecc528d9d "Keyboard Left System key.") is "Left Meta" on Linux, "Left Windows" on Windows and "Left Command" on macOS.

The current keyboard layout set by the operating system is used to interpret the scancode: for example, [sf::Keyboard::Key::Semicolon](#acb4cacd7cc5802dec45724cf3314a142a9806fa37a3ecd39bf637c203aa011ed0 "The ; key.") is mapped to ";" for layout and to "é" for others.

Parameters
:   |  |  |
    | --- | --- |
    | code | [Scancode](#a51f3be2ef1d778bd470c35f0ed39b0ba) to check |

Returns
:   The localized description of the code

## Detailed Description

The audio listener is the point in the scene from where all the sounds are heard.

The audio listener defines the global properties of the audio environment, it defines where and how sounds and musics are heard.

If [sf::View](classsf_1_1View.html "2D camera that defines what region is shown on screen") is the eyes of the user, then [sf::Listener](namespacesf_1_1Listener.html "The audio listener is the point in the scene from where all the sounds are heard.") are their ears (by the way, they are often linked together – same position, orientation, etc.).

[sf::Listener](namespacesf_1_1Listener.html "The audio listener is the point in the scene from where all the sounds are heard.") is a simple interface, which allows to setup the listener in the 3D audio environment (position, direction and up vector), and to adjust the global volume.

Usage example:

// Move the listener to the position (1, 0, -5)

[sf::Listener::setPosition](#a3eeab65603414a8267e3ed8554dd2843)({1, 0, -5});

// Make it face the right axis (1, 0, 0)

[sf::Listener::setDirection](#a6d10105ab58a9529cd23b84ebf9cb0ee)({1, 0, 0});

// Reduce the global volume

[sf::Listener::setGlobalVolume](#a7da4d76ecdca02cabbd2233caf60f7e3)(50);

[sf::Listener::setPosition](#a3eeab65603414a8267e3ed8554dd2843)

void setPosition(const Vector3f &position)

Set the position of the listener in the scene.

[sf::Listener::setDirection](#a6d10105ab58a9529cd23b84ebf9cb0ee)

void setDirection(const Vector3f &direction)

Set the forward vector of the listener in the scene.

[sf::Listener::setGlobalVolume](#a7da4d76ecdca02cabbd2233caf60f7e3)

## Detailed Description

Give access to the real-time state of the mouse.

[sf::Mouse](namespacesf_1_1Mouse.html "Give access to the real-time state of the mouse.") provides an interface to the state of the mouse.

A single mouse is assumed.

This namespace allows users to query the mouse state at any time and directly, without having to deal with a window and its events. Compared to the MouseMoved, MouseButtonPressed and MouseButtonReleased events, [sf::Mouse](namespacesf_1_1Mouse.html "Give access to the real-time state of the mouse.") can retrieve the state of the cursor and the buttons at any time (you don't need to store and update a boolean on your side in order to know if a button is pressed or released), and you always get the real state of the mouse, even if it is moved, pressed or released when your window is out of focus and no event is triggered.

The setPosition and getPosition functions can be used to change or retrieve the current position of the mouse pointer. There are two versions: one that operates in global coordinates (relative to the desktop) and one that operates in window coordinates (relative to a specific window).

Usage example:

if ([sf::Mouse::isButtonPressed](#a2c04cfb3777a682cd83629ab0ba7443d)([sf::Mouse::Button::Left](#a4fb128be433f9aafe66bc0c605daaa90a945d5e233cf7d6240f6b783b36a374ff)))

{

// left click...

}

// get global mouse position

[sf::Vector2i](namespacesf.html#af0ffe1b157a56931ee3a9a1a771a827a) position = [sf::Mouse::getPosition](#ad662f5ffc4b5b8c395be6a58d482b5fb)();

// set mouse position relative to a window

[sf::Mouse::setPosition](#a6cf7dc4def89a2ae4e954fe0f454fed5)([sf::Vector2i](namespacesf.html#af0ffe1b157a56931ee3a9a1a771a827a)(100, 200), window);

## Function Documentation

## [◆](#afb84033768d8be76f1820886f5aa1003)getAvailableDevices()

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| |  |  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | std::vector< std::string > sf::PlaybackDevice::getAvailableDevices | ( |  | ) |  | | nodiscard |

Get a list of the names of all available audio playback devices.

This function returns a vector of strings containing the names of all available audio playback devices.

If the operating system reports multiple devices with the same name, a number will be appended to the name of all subsequent devices to distinguish them from each other. This guarantees that every entry returned by this function will represent a unique device.

For example, if the operating system reports multiple devices with the name "Sound Card", the entries returned would be:

* [Sound](classsf_1_1Sound.html "Regular sound that can be played in the audio environment.") Card
* [Sound](classsf_1_1Sound.html "Regular sound that can be played in the audio environment.") Card 2
* [Sound](classsf_1_1Sound.html "Regular sound that can be played in the audio environment.") Card 3
* ...

The default device, if one is marked as such, will be placed at the beginning of the vector.

If no devices are available, this function will return an empty vector.

Returns
:   A vector of strings containing the device names or an empty vector if no devices are available

## Detailed Description

Give access to the real-time state of the sensors.

[sf::Sensor](namespacesf_1_1Sensor.html "Give access to the real-time state of the sensors.") provides an interface to the state of the various sensors that a device provides.

This namespace allows users to query the sensors values at any time and directly, without having to deal with a window and its events. Compared to the SensorChanged event, [sf::Sensor](namespacesf_1_1Sensor.html "Give access to the real-time state of the sensors.") can retrieve the state of a sensor at any time (you don't need to store and update its current value on your side).

Depending on the OS and hardware of the device (phone, tablet, ...), some sensor types may not be available. You should always check the availability of a sensor before trying to read it, with the [sf::Sensor::isAvailable](#a8bcd2db34212d34bd1a1365a029674b1 "Check if a sensor is available on the underlying platform.") function.

You may wonder why some sensor types look so similar, for example Accelerometer and Gravity / UserAcceleration. The first one is the raw measurement of the acceleration, and takes into account both the earth gravity and the user movement. The others are more precise: they provide these components separately, which is usually more useful. In fact they are not direct sensors, they are computed internally based on the raw acceleration and other sensors. This is exactly the same for Gyroscope vs Orientation.

Because sensors consume a non-negligible amount of current, they are all disabled by default. You must call [sf::Sensor::setEnabled](#abae92d8aec41b231ac1f12d007806b99 "Enable or disable a sensor.") for each sensor in which you are interested.

Usage example:

if ([sf::Sensor::isAvailable](#a8bcd2db34212d34bd1a1365a029674b1)([sf::Sensor::Type::Gravity](#a687375af3ab77b818fca73735bcaea84a8a88c39cef668fb55f188af09665bd40)))

{

// gravity sensor is available

}

// enable the gravity sensor

[sf::Sensor::setEnabled](#abae92d8aec41b231ac1f12d007806b99)([sf::Sensor::Type::Gravity](#a687375af3ab77b818fca73735bcaea84a8a88c39cef668fb55f188af09665bd40), true);

// get the current value of gravity

[sf::Vector3f](namespacesf.html#aabc495912efba35400b484ea842664d0) gravity = [sf::Sensor::getValue](#a17ccc6f0906d33255ccf1bb777669046)([sf::Sensor::Type::Gravity](#a687375af3ab77b818fca73735bcaea84a8a88c39cef668fb55f188af09665bd40));

## Detailed Description

Give access to the real-time state of the touches.

[sf::Touch](namespacesf_1_1Touch.html "Give access to the real-time state of the touches.") provides an interface to the state of the touches.

This namespace allows users to query the touches state at any time and directly, without having to deal with a window and its events. Compared to the TouchBegan, TouchMoved and TouchEnded events, [sf::Touch](namespacesf_1_1Touch.html "Give access to the real-time state of the touches.") can retrieve the state of the touches at any time (you don't need to store and update a boolean on your side in order to know if a touch is down), and you always get the real state of the touches, even if they happen when your window is out of focus and no event is triggered.

The getPosition function can be used to retrieve the current position of a touch. There are two versions: one that operates in global coordinates (relative to the desktop) and one that operates in window coordinates (relative to a specific window).

Touches are identified by an index (the "finger"), so that in multi-touch events, individual touches can be tracked correctly. As long as a finger touches the screen, it will keep the same index even if other fingers start or stop touching the screen in the meantime. As a consequence, active touch indices may not always be sequential (i.e. touch number 0 may be released while touch number 1 is still down).

Usage example:

if ([sf::Touch::isDown](#a16ec0dde98706dcd9144a4263466571a)(0))

{

// touch 0 is down

}

// get global position of touch 1

[sf::Vector2i](namespacesf.html#af0ffe1b157a56931ee3a9a1a771a827a) globalPos = [sf::Touch::getPosition](#ae5d31f537862622b3bd0fa738ba37d43)(1);

// get position of touch 1 relative to a window

[sf::Vector2i](namespacesf.html#af0ffe1b157a56931ee3a9a1a771a827a) relativePos = [sf::Touch::getPosition](#ae5d31f537862622b3bd0fa738ba37d43)(1, window);

[Vulkan](namespacesf_1_1Vulkan.html "Vulkan helper functions.") helper functions.

This namespace contains functions to help you use SFML for windowing and write your own [Vulkan](namespacesf_1_1Vulkan.html "Vulkan helper functions.") code for graphics.
